content: The Azure Logic Apps updates for September and October 2019 include features, connector updates, and announcements about regional deployments. New features File System Connector preview available in Integration Service Environment Visual Studio support for logic apps in Integration Service Environment New Azure Advisor recommendation for logic apps not firing when trigger fails Lazy IF expression evaluation Client certificate authentication for actions relaxed password requirement constraint Managed identity support for Azure Functions, Azure API Management, and Azure App Services actions Logic Apps definition parameters can be found as tokens in token picker Azure Blob Storage connector can be used to access Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 storage accounts New regions France Korea South Africa Connectors that became generally available Azure Container Instances Azure Data Factory New connectors Azure Monitor Logs GoFileRoom IntegrablePDF Cloudmersive Document Conversion Company Connect ModuleQ FireText zReports Mitto SparkPost SigningHub Vantage365 Imaging EasyVista Self Help Huddle Seismic Elfsquad Product Configurator Pushcut Envoy HotProfile JungleMail 365 New connectors deployed to US Gov Cloud Plumsail Documents Plumsail Helpdesk Plumsail SP Plumsail Forms Cloudmersive Virus Scan

title: Azure Site Recovery update rollup 42—November 2019
content: This update provides fixes and download links to the latest versions of these Site Recovery components: Site Recovery Unified Setup and Site Recovery Mobility agent (both version 9.30.5407.1) for Windows Server, CentOS, and Ubuntu machines. Used for Azure virtual machine (VM) replication, and replication of on-premises VMware VMs and physical servers to Azure. Site Recovery configuration server OVF template (version 5.1.5200.0). Used for replication of on-premises VMware VMs and physical servers to Azure. Site Recovery Provider (version 5.1.5200). Used for replication of Hyper-V VMs to Azure. Recovery Services agent (version 2.0.9165.0). Used for replication of Hyper-V VMs to Azure. Read more information .

title: HPC Specialized VMs - HB and HC-series
content: We are pleased to announce we are deploying HB and HC Virtual Machines to additional regions The HB-Series VM is now available in East US. The HC-Series VM is now available in Japan East. The HB-series VMs are optimized for HPC applications driven by memory bandwidth, such as fluid dynamics, explicit finite element analysis, and weather modeling. HC-series VMs are optimized for HPC applications driven by intensive computation, such as implicit finite element analysis, reservoir simulation, and computational chemistry. See regional availability for Azure Virtual Machines here . Learn more

title: New Azure policies to manage certificates across your organization, currently in preview
content: Large organizations have thousands of certificates in key vaults distributed across thousands of applications and subscriptions. If you are responsible for security and compliance across the organization, you need a simple way to set rules across all these certificates, prove that those rules were followed, and flag violations. Azure policy helps with this. We have added new policies in preview for certificates in Azure Key Vault. Issuer Policy: Flag certificates that are (or are not) issued by a particular issuer. Key Type Policy: Flag certificates that are (or are not) protected by a RSA or ECC key pairs. Key Size Policy: Flag certificates that are (or are not protected) by a key of a certain size. Expiry Policy: Flag certificates that are (or are not) renewed within “X” number of days of their expiry date. Validity Lifespan Policy: Flag certificates that have (or do not have) Validity Lifespan that is less than, or more than, or equal to "X" number of years. Learn more

title: Azure Key Vault Virtual Machine extension now generally available
content: The Azure Key Vault Virtual Machine extension makes it easier for apps running on virtual machines to use certificates from a key vault, by abstracting the common tasks as well as best practices—authenticate, handle common network errors, cache, periodically refresh the certificate from the key vault, and bind the certificate for Transport Layer Security (TLS). This extension is now generally available for Windows and Linux . Linux Learn More Windows Learn More

title: Azure Disk Encryption in more places, and more services offering customer-managed keys
content: Azure Disk Encryption enables you to encrypt your Azure Virtual Machine disks with your keys safeguarded in Azure Key Vault. Previously this capability was available through PowerShell and CLI. We have now added this capability to the Azure portal, which makes it very easy to use. We have also added support for the latest versions of the common Linux distros on Azure, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7.6 and 7.7 as well as CentOS Linux 7.6 and 7.7. The following services recently announced preview for customer-managed keys for encryption at rest. Azure Event Hubs Azure Managed Disks Power BI For a full list of services offering encryption with customer-managed keys, see the Azure Data Encryption-at-Rest documentation page . Quickstart for Linux Quickstart for Windows

title: Extension of Customer Lockbox for Microsoft Azure beyond virtual machines
content: Customer Lockbox provides customers the capability to control Azure support engineers' access to workloads that contain customer data This expanded support now provides customers control over access to their data for a larger set of Azure offerings. New services and scenarios, available in preview: Azure Storage Azure SQL Database Azure Data Explorer Memory dumps and managed disks for Azure Virtual Machines Transferring Azure subscriptions Sign up Learn more

title: Release of Microsoft Secure Code Analysis toolkit to help you build secure code
content: With the Microsoft Security Code Analysis extension, you can infuse security analysis tools including Credential Scanner, BinSkim, and others into your Azure DevOps continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) pipelines. Increase developer productivity and simplify security through easily configurable build tasks that abstract away the complexities (installing, updating, maintaining, and running) from analysis tools without relinquishing control over them. This product is now available via Unified Support. Customers can sign up using their existing credit or paying the service fee. Learn more

title: Threat Protection for Azure Key Vault in Public Preview in North America Regions
content: Azure Key Vault is an essential service for protecting data and improving performance of cloud applications by offering the ability to centrally manage keys, secrets, cryptographic keys and policies in the cloud. Since Azure Key Vault stores sensitive and business critical data, it requires maximum security for the key vaults and the data stored in them. Azure Security Center’s support for Threat Protection for Azure Key Vault provides an additional layer of security intelligence that detects unusual and potentially harmful attempts to access or exploit key vaults. This new layer of protection allows customers to address threats against their key vaults without being a security expert or manage security monitoring systems. The feature is in public preview in North America Regions. Learn more

title: Threat Protection for Azure Storage includes Malware Reputation Screening
content: Threat protection for Azure Storage offers new detections powered by Microsoft Threat Intelligence for detecting malware uploads to Azure Storage using hash reputation analysis and suspicious access from an active Tor exit node (an anonymizing proxy). You can now view detected malware across storage accounts using Azure Security Center. Learn more

title: Azure Container Registry repository-scoped RBAC permissions are now in preview
content: Announcing the public preview of repository-scoped RBAC permissions for Azure Container Registry (ACR). ACR already supported several authentication options using identities that have role-based access to an entire registry. However, for certain scenarios, customers might want to limit the access to specific repositories in a registry. Token based repository permissions now enable this functionality. Learn more

title: Azure Container Registry—Diagnostic logs are now in preview
content: Diagnostic logs for Azure Container Registry are now in preview. Logs are available for: Authentication and repository-level events for registry authentication events and status. Operations such as push and pull for images and other artifacts in registry repositories. Container registry metrics such as aggregated push and pull counts. Learn more

title: New Azure Advisor recommendation category: operational excellence
content: Azure Advisor is launching a new category of recommendations called operational excellence . This new category will help you follow best practices for process and workflow efficiency, resource manageability, and deployment. Azure Advisor now offers a new category of recommendations called operational excellence to help you follow best practices for process and workflow efficiency, resource manageability, and deployment. These recommendations are available in the operational excellence tab of the Advisor dashboard. They’re also available via Advisor’s CLI and API . The operational excellence category is launching with nine recommendations, and more are on the way. Examples include creating Azure Service Health alerts to be notified when Azure service issues affect you; repairing invalid log alert rules; and following best practices using Azure policy, such as tag management, geo-compliance requirements, and specifying permitted VM SKUs for deployment. Together, these recommendations will help you optimize your cloud operations practices. For more information on Advisor’s operational excellence recommendations, see the documentation . Azure Advisor in the Azure portal Azure Advisor documentation Azure Advisor feedback

title: Migrate SQL Server databases for Windows users to SQL managed instance
content: Support is now available in preview for T-SQL Data Definition Language (DDL) for Windows users and groups migrating from SQL Server databases to SQL managed instance with Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) authentication. The engine support provided enables a manual migration using T-SQL Data Definition Language (DDL) commands executed after restoring a SQL Server database on SQL managed instance. For users who consider a migration from SQL Server to SQL managed instance, this feature helps map Windows users and groups to Azure AD users and groups. All permissions and database-role memberships will be retained for the migrated database users. Learn more about this announcement .

title: GitHub Actions for Azure are now generally available
content: GitHub Actions , now generally available, make it possible to create simple, yet powerful workflows to automate software compilation and delivery, and are integrated with GitHub. These actions, defined in YAML files, allow you to trigger an automated workflow process on any GitHub event, such as code commits, creation of pull requests, or new GitHub releases. See all the GitHub Actions for Azure and their repositories, along with documentation and sample templates to help you easily create workflows to build, test, package, release, and deploy to Azure, following a push or pull request. Easily create GitHub CI/CD workflows targeting Azure using Azure starter templates . Use them to deploy apps created with popular languages and frameworks such as .NET, Node.js, Java, PHP, Ruby or Python, in containers or running on any operating system. Learn more

title: Azure Database for PostgreSQL - Hyperscale (Citus)—User role management is now available
content: Now in general availability, user role management enables management of Postgres user roles on Hyperscale (Citus) server group nodes in addition to "citus" and other built-in roles. You now have the ability to create and delete additional user roles as well as reset passwords for these roles in the Azure portal. All Postgres roles defined are valid on all coordinator and worker nodes in the Hyperscale (Citus) server group. Role privileges can be modified using standard Postgres commands and tools such as PgAdmin or psql. System-wide GRANTs can be propagated to all nodes using run_command_on_workers() helper function. Learn more

title: Azure Database for PostgreSQL - Hyperscale (Citus)—64 vCore compute option is now available
content: Now in general availability, Hyperscale (Citus) supports a 64 vCore compute option in addition to the 4, 8, 16, and 32 vCore choices previously available. Compute options can be selected separately for coordinator and worker nodes within a Hyperscale (Citus) server group and can be selected when Hyperscale (Citus) cluster is created or modified on existing clusters. With the 64 vCore option now available, coordinator nodes can get as much as 256 GiB RAM, whereas worker nodes can get up to 512 GiB RAM. Learn more

title: Azure Database for PostgreSQL - Hyperscale (Citus)—High availability (HA) is now generally available
content: Now in general availability, high availability (HA) for Azure Database for PostgreSQL - Hyperscale (Citus) allows for minimal database downtime by maintaining standby replicas of every node in a server group. If a node goes down, Hyperscale (Citus) switches incoming connections from the failed node to its standby. Failover happens within a few minutes, and promoted nodes always have fresh data through PostgreSQL synchronous streaming replication. Learn more

title: Migrate from Bing Speech to Speech Services and the Speech SDK by January 14, 2020
content: We’re extending the Bing Speech retirement date to January 14, 2020. Bing Speech API will continue supporting your applications until January 14, 2020. However, we encourage you to migrate to Speech Services and the Speech SDK as soon as possible to enjoy their rich benefits including: Speech-to-text (speech recognition), intent, translation, and text-to-speech capabilities. Batch transcription capability through a dedicated REST API. A larger set of adaptable locales, new and more accurate models, and improved modes of interaction. Contact us Learn more about migrating your Bing Speech application to Speech .

title: Azure Data Box heavy edition now available for petabyte-sized data transfers
content: The Azure Data Box heavy edition is a secure, ruggedized appliance shipped to customers to facilitate petabyte-sized offline data transfers to Azure Storage. Data Box makes data migration to Azure fast and simple by providing a secure, tamper-resistant method for quick transfer of your data. You can order the Data Box through the Azure portal . Easily connect it to your existing network, then load your data onto Data Box using standard NAS protocols (SMB/CIFS). Your data is automatically protected using 256-AES encryption. Data Box is returned to the Azure Data Center to be uploaded to Azure, then the device is securely erased. Learn more .

title: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Single Server—Reserved capacity is now available
content: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Single Server reserved capacity is now available to reserve compute power for your existing and future PostgreSQL servers. The new pricing option enables you to save up to 49 percent compared to the regular pay-as-you-go payment option for your PostgreSQL server vCores for a one-year period. Read more about this announcement in our service documentation . For more information, see the Azure Database for PostgreSQL pricing page .

title: Azure Database for MariaDB—Reserved capacity is now available
content: Azure Database for MariaDB reserved capacity is now available to reserve compute power for your existing and future MariaDB servers. The new pricing option enables you to save up to 51 percent compared to the regular pay-as-you-go payment option for your MariaDB server vCores for a one-year period. Read more about this announcement in our service documentation . For more information, see the Azure Database for MariaDB pricing page .

title: Azure Database for MySQL—Reserved capacity is now available
content: Azure Database for MySQL reserved capacity is now available to reserve compute power for your existing and future MySQL servers. This new pricing option enables you to save up to 51 percent compared to the regular pay-as-you-go payment option for your MySQL server vCores for a one-year period. Read more about this announcement in our service documentation . For more information, see the Azure Database for MySQL pricing page .

title: Azure CDN Standard Rules Engine preview update
content: Earlier this summer, we launched Azure CDN Standard rules engine with ARM and PowerShell support for Azure CDN from Microsoft. Rules Engine allows you to control CDN behavior on a per HTTP request basis, to optimize your workloads based on your customer needs. This week we’re announcing that portal support is now available as part of this preview. You can now customize your Content Delivery Network behavior quickly and easily in just a few steps in the Azure Portal. Learn more

title: Large storage for Azure Database for PostgreSQL–Single is now available
content: Azure Database for PostgreSQL–Single now has support for up to 16 TB of storage and up to 20,000 IOPS. With this functionality, you get five times more storage for database servers, as well as more than triple the available IOPS. This ensures that you can run your most demanding, large scale workloads on Azure Database for PostgreSQL-Single server. Learn more in the related service detail .

title: Azure Database for MySQL—Large storage is now generally available
content: Support is now available for up to 16 TB of storage and up to 20,000 IOPS in Azure Database services for MySQL. With this functionality, you not only get five times more storage for database servers, but also more than triple the available IOPS. This ensures that you can run your most demanding, large scale workloads on Azure Database services for MySQL. Learn more in the related service detail .

title: Azure Synapse Analytics—Continuous integration and deployment with SSDT is now available
content: The highest requested feature for Azure Synapse Analytics is now available— SQL Server Data Tools (SSDT) Database projects . This release includes support for SSDT with Visual Studio 2019, along with native platform integration with Azure DevOps, providing built-in continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) capabilities for enterprise level deployments. Data engineers and developers can integrate their SSDT database project with Azure Repos where check-ins can be pre-validated using tools such as MSBuild. Set up stable release pipelines without any custom code. Use Azure Pipelines to automatically promote changes to your data warehouse model more safely across development, testing, and production environments. These improvements help provide a frictionless development and deployment experience for your analytics platform. Learn more . Install Visual Studio 2019 for SQL Analytics to get started. Set up source control integration with SQL Analytics by using Azure Repos. Integrate a simple Azure Pipeline for continuous integration and deployment with for SQL analytics within Azure Synapse.

title: Azure DevOps—New sprint burndown widget and improved pipelines security
content: Azure Repos: Cross-repo branch policy administration Azure Pipelines: Multi-stage pipelines UX Orchestrate canary deployment strategy on environment for Kubernetes Approval policies for YAML pipelines Azure Container Registry as a first-class pipeline resource Pipeline resource meta-data as predefined variables Traceability for pipelines and Azure Container Registry resources Simplified resource authorization in YAML pipelines Improve pipeline security by restricting the scope of access tokens Evaluate artifact check Markdown support in automated test error messages Diagnosing cron schedules in YAML Updates to the Azure Resource Manager template deployment task Project level security for service connections Ubuntu 18.04 pool Service Mesh Interface based canary deployments in KubernetesManifest task ReviewApp in Environment Azure Artifacts: Updated Connect to feed experience Public feeds are now generally available with upstream support Create project-scoped feeds from the portal Reporting: A sprint burndown widget with everything you've been asking for Wiki: Synchronous scroll for editing wiki pages Page visits for wiki pages In the latest Azure DevOps update, we added a new sprint burndown widget that supports burning down by story points, count of tasks, and by summing custom fields. In addition, we improved pipelines security by restricting the scope of access tokens. Check out the features list for more updates and improvements.

title: Azure Data Factory has added Avro and CosmosDB to data flows
content: CosmosDB and Avro formats are now available natively in Data Factory's data flows. Use mapping data flows with your hierarchical, array, and complex data to generate and execute data transformation at scale. Full transformation capabilities are supported, including aggregations, pivots, joins, and calculate columns, among others. CosmosDB also includes dynamic throughput scale-up during ETL processes, as well as full support for document updates, upserts, inserts, and deletes. Learn more .

title: Azure Stream Analytics—Real-time scoring with custom machine learning models
content: Azure Stream Analytics now supports high-performance, real-time scoring by taking advantage of custom pre-trained machine learning models that are managed by Azure Machine Learning service and hosted in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) or Azure Container Instances, using a workflow that doesn't require users to write any code. Build custom models by using any popular python libraries such as Scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow, and more to train your models anywhere including Azure Databricks, Azure Machine Learning Compute, and HD Insight. Once deployed in AKS or Container Instances clusters, you can use Stream Analytics to surface all end points within the job itself. Sign up for a private preview of this feature now.

title: Azure Database for MySQL support for intelligent performance is now available
content: Azure Database for MySQL support for the intelligent performance set of features, which includes query store , query performance insight , and performance recommendations , is now generally available. This set of features provides the ability for you to better understand your workloads, including the ability to visually inspect them, and to identify bottlenecks. Use this functionality to view a list of recommendations for improving the performance of your workloads. Learn more about performance recommendations for Azure Database for MySQL . Learn more about query performance insight for Azure Database for MySQL . Learn more about query store for Azure Database for MySQL .
