content: Azure Blob storage accounts with hot and cool storage tiers are generally available in our Canadian regions: Canada Central and Canada East. You can find the updated list of available regions on the Azure services by region page. Blob storage accounts are specialized storage accounts for storing your unstructured data as blobs (objects) in Azure Storage. With Blob storage accounts, you can choose between hot and cool storage tiers to store your less frequently accessed (cool) data at a lower storage cost, and store more frequently accessed (hot) data at a lower access cost. Customers in the new regions can take advantage of the cost benefits of the cool storage tier for storing backup data, media content, scientific data, active archival data—and in general, any data that is less frequently accessed. For details on how to start using this feature, please see our getting-started documentation . For details on regional pricing, see the Azure Storage pricing page.

title: General availability of IaaS migration from classic to Resource Manager
content: Today we're announcing the general availability of platform-managed IaaS migration of resources from the classic deployment model to the Azure Resource Manager deployment model. All migration functionality that was released as a preview on May 12 is now generally available. Storage account migration from classic to Resource Manager is also generally available.

title: Azure Cosmos DB capacity planner update
content: To continue helping customers fine-tune their Azure Cosmos DB throughput and storage estimations, we've updated the Azure Cosmos DB capacity planner tool with support for document update operations and data storage calculations. For more information about Azure Cosmos DB, visit the Azure Cosmos DB page .

title: Point-in-time restore retention for Standard tier extended to 35 days
content: For Azure SQL Database, we automatically take backups so you can restore from the unintended deletion or modification of data. We're excited to announce that all Standard-tier databases and Standard-tier elastic database pools now have 35 days of retention built in, at no extra charge. This change reflects our goal of providing a consistent user experience across service tiers. Next steps: Learn more about Azure SQL Database business continuity features . Learn how to restore an Azure SQL database to a point in time .

title: Generally available: Windows 10 Enterprise State Roaming via Azure Active Directory Premium
content: Generally available as a feature of Azure Active Directory Premium, Enterprise State Roaming in Windows 10 gives users a unified experience across devices. It allows the use of work or school identities to synchronize user settings and modern app data by using the Azure cloud for storage. Enterprise users are protected from the loss of modern app data due to hardware failure, theft, or device replacement. Enterprises benefit from enhanced security and better control on the enterprise data. All data is encrypted with Azure Rights Management before leaving the device. For more information, please visit the Enterprise State Roaming overview documentation page.

title: Preview of Service Fabric on Linux
content: At Build 2016, we announced a limited preview of Azure Service Fabric on Linux, which you can use to build, deploy, and manage cloud applications by using the same core technology that Microsoft has used to build massively scalable solutions on Windows. With this preview, you can create ​Reliable Actors and stateless Reliable Services in Java on top of our runtime. Developers can build apps by using the tools with which they're familiar, including Yeoman scaffolding, Gradle builds, and Vagrant-based setup. The SDK and runtime also provide support for containers and guest executables, as well as the ability to create and deploy apps to a cluster on Azure or your development computer. Please feel free to sign up for our preview and try things out. If you want to know more, this blog discusses how we got the product running on Linux, some of the forks we had to take, and how we made those decisions.

title: New Azure Mobile Engagement SDKs for Xamarin, Unity, and web (preview) available
content: You can now integrate Azure Mobile Engagement in your apps if you are developing for Xamarin.iOS or Xamarin.Android by using our Xamarin SDK . You can also integrate Azure Mobile Engagement if you are writing a gaming app by using our Unity SDK. Documentation is available for iOS and Android . And finally, we have released a preview of the Web SDK . You can use this SDK to collect analytics in a way that's similar to what Azure Mobile Engagement does. There is no support for sending push notifications at the moment with the Web SDK.

title: General availability: Azure cool blob storage in new regions
content: Azure Blob storage accounts with hot and cool storage tiers are generally available in three additional regions: South Central US, Asia East, and Australia East. You can find the updated list of available regions on the Azure services by region page. Blob storage accounts are specialized storage accounts for storing your unstructured data as blobs (objects) in Azure Storage. With Blob storage accounts, you can choose between hot and cool storage tiers to store your less frequently accessed (cool) data at a lower storage cost, and store more frequently accessed (hot) data at a lower access cost. Customers in the new regions can take advantage of the cost benefits of the cool storage tier for storing backup data, media content, scientific data, active archival data—and in general, any data that is less frequently accessed. For details on how to start using this feature, please see our getting-started documentation . For details on regional pricing, see the Azure Storage pricing page.

title: Release of Service Fabric SDK 2.1.150 and runtime 5.1.150
content: Azure Service Fabric SDK 2.1.150 has been released. This release includes new features and important bug fixes. You can get the updated SDK from the following links: Runtime, SDK, and tools for Visual Studio 2015 (requires Visual Studio 2015 Update 2 ) Runtime, SDK, and tools for Visual Studio “15” Preview Runtime and SDK only (no tools) An update to the preview of the standalone installer for Windows Server has also been released, based on runtime 5.1.150. For more information, see the release announcement on the Service Fabric team blog.

title: Two more things to keep your cost on track in DevTest Labs
content: A few months back, we released our first cost-management feature in Azure DevTest Labs: monthly cost trend. You can use it to see how much you have spent in the current calendar month and to get a projection of the spending till the month end, based on your spending in the last seven days. Since then, we moved to the second question you probably have in your mind: Why is lab spending so fast? To help you to get a clear answer, we have released a new feature. The feature makes your life easier by showing you the month-to-date cost per resource in a table. We have also released a feature that you can use to set the target lab cost for the current calendar month. The target cost will appear in the “Monthly estimated cost trend” chart. This chart will help you track the month-to-date lab spending relative to the target cost for the current month, so you can identify if you are going to exceed your budget for the month. For more details on these features, please check out the post in our team blog. Please try the new features and let us know how can we make them better by sharing your ideas and suggestions at the DevTest Labs feedback forum . If you run into any problems with the features or have any questions, we are always ready to help you at our MSDN forum .

title: General availability: Git integration for API Management
content: The Git integration feature for Azure API Management has been in preview for a couple of months. We have received great feedback and made some improvements to it. We are delighted to announce that the feature is now generally available. For more information about Git integration, see the article How to save and configure your API Management service configuration using Git .

title: Scale data across the globe with Azure Cosmos DB multiple-region replication
content: The global distribution capability of Azure Cosmos DB is generally available in all Azure Cosmos DB regions. You can use Azure Cosmos DB to associate any number of Azure regions to your database account. Azure Cosmos DB transparently distributes your data across all the regions associated with your database account and offers provisioned throughput , well-defined consistency choices , and low-latency and availability guarantees. It also offers transparent failover with multi-homing APIs . With the support for multiple-region replication in Azure Cosmos DB, you can develop applications that require global access to data, and you can set up seamless failover for regions in the event of actual or simulated failures. You can configure Azure Cosmos DB to elastically scale throughput and storage across the globe in in less than a minute through the Azure portal . Read the Distribute data globally with Azure Cosmos DB article for more information.

title: New capabilities available on the Azure Batch service
content: In the past few months, we've added many new capabilities to the Azure Batch service, including: Support for Linux compute nodes . Support for MPI workloads on Windows . Support for application packages . Support for task dependencies . Configurable autoscale interval. Client libraries for Python, Java, and Node.js . Azure CLI support (Xplat-CLI). Additionally, we've made many improvements to the new Azure portal experience for Batch, including: The ability to create, update, and delete pools of compute nodes from the portal. The ability to create, run, and terminate jobs and tasks from the portal. The ability to see task logs from the portal. Creation and management of application packages. Improved compute node management (delete, reimage, connect). Support for linked storage accounts. Visit our documentation page to learn more about these new features and everything else that's available to you with Batch.

title: Azure Site Recovery: Scout 8.0.1 Update 3 is available
content: Scout 8.0.1 Update 3 is a cumulative update for Azure Site Recovery that contains Update 1, Update 2, and new fixes. You can apply Update 3 directly on Scout 8.0.1 in general availability. To learn more about Update 3 fixes, and to get download and installation instructions, see the Replicate on-premises VMware virtual machines or physical servers to a secondary site article.

title: Azure Search: Update to the Search Traffic Analytics dashboard in Power BI
content: The new Power BI content pack for Azure Search contains insightful data about your Azure Search service and useful visualizations. You can use the content pack to learn about service traffic, including queries per second (QPS) and information about throttled search queries. To create your new dashboard, visit the Content packs for Power BI page and enter the search service name and the credentials to the storage account that's associated with Search Traffic Analytics. If you don't have Search Traffic Analytics enabled for your Azure Search service, you can learn more in the Enabling and using Search Traffic Analytics article. If you want to learn more about Azure Search, see the What is Azure Search? article.

title: Batch send notifications to device tokens using Notification Hubs
content: We're excited to announce the Batch Direct Send feature for Azure Notification Hubs customers at the Basic and Standard tiers. This is a batch version of the previously published Direct Send feature, which enables the sending of notifications to individual device tokens and channel URIs. Because this feature doesn't require devices to be registered with Notification Hubs, customers can use their hubs as scalable push engines at their convenience. This simplifies custom device storage and migration scenarios. See the full details and a sample in the blog post .

title: Support for Azure Active Directory B2C
content: We've added initial support for using Azure App Service Authentication/Authorization (also know as Easy Auth) with Azure Active Directory B2C policies. For more information, see the detailed blog post .

title: Azure Search S3 and S3 High Density tiers in public preview, and Basic tier generally available
content: We’ve introduced new Standard tier options into public preview: S3 and S3 High Density. The Basic tier is now generally available. Azure Search helps developers build rich, first-class search experiences into their applications. Bring your data and a few lines of code, and Azure Search takes care of the rest. With these new options, it’s even easier to start and grow with Azure Search. Compared to S2, the S3 tier delivers double the storage and number of documents hosted within your Azure Search service, and it offers lower latency for large datasets. S3 High Density lets customers deliver unique search experiences within applications that support a multitenant environment. The new High Density option allows a large number of indexes within a single service while maintaining data isolation between tenants in your application, making it ideal for high-volume SaaS scenarios. This enables you to scale your application’s rich search capabilities while isolating data and search results for each customer. For more information, please visit the Azure blog and the Azure Search pricing page.

title: Azure API Management is available in Canada regions
content: We are delighted to announce that Azure API Management is live in the Canada East and Canada Central regions. API Management can now be deployed to 20 regions around the world!

title: Run your own custom Automation tasks in response to VM alerts
content: When you create an alert rule on a virtual machine, you can now choose to run a custom task (Azure Automation runbook) when the alert is triggered. In March, we released the ability for you to choose a standard task, like restarting or stopping the VM. Today, we extend this functionality so you can choose one of your custom Automation runbooks to respond to the VM alert with your own workflow steps. Also, you can choose to vertically scale the VM up or down based on the VM alert rule. These two tasks have been added to the Standard task list: Scale Up VM and Scale Down VM . For more information about using Automation runbooks to respond to virtual machine alerts, see this article .

title: Azure Redis Cache: Preview of import/export and scale to Premium tier
content: The Azure Redis Cache team is pleased to announce the following updates: You can use the import/export data-management operation to import data into Azure Redis Cache or export data from Azure Redis Cache. For more information and a step-by-step guide, see Import and export data in Azure Redis Cache . You can scale to the Premium tier. For more information and a step-by-step guide, see How to scale Azure Redis Cache .

title: Namespace-level tier selection enabled for Notification Hubs
content: Azure Notification Hubs recently enabled namespace-level tiers . Each subscription used to have all of its namespaces and hubs tied to one tier (free, basic, or standard), but that wasn't the most efficient way for our customers to handle resources. With namespace-level tiers, customers can allocate resources tailored to each namespace’s expected traffic and usage patterns. See the full details in the blog post .

title: Deploy geo-fenced push notifications by using Azure Notification Hubs
content: We published a tutorial that explains how to deliver location-based push notifications by using Azure Notification Hubs and Bing Spatial Data Services, leveraged from within a Universal Windows Platform application. Learn more in our official article .

title: Automation: New graphical runbook type based on native PowerShell
content: In Azure Automation, you can now create graphical runbooks that are based on native PowerShell. This means that graphical runbooks you create will start very quickly and will be easier to author and test. If you need checkpointing in your workflows, you can still create "Graphical PowerShell Workflow" runbooks. These have been renamed from their previous "Graphical" name. There are new icons for the runbook types to help you quickly identify them, and the authoring canvas for graphical runbooks has a new look. To get started with graphical runbooks, you can convert one of your existing Graphical PowerShell Workflow runbooks to a graphical runbook by exporting it and then re-importing as the new type. You can also easily get started by importing new graphical runbooks from the Automation Runbook Gallery (Script Center source).

title: Automation Runbook Gallery update
content: The Azure Automation Runbook Gallery now pulls runbook content from the PowerShell Gallery in addition to Script Center. To find scripts from the PowerShell Gallery, navigate to your Automation account > Runbooks , and then click the Browse Gallery command. After the gallery and filter blades have opened, you can use Gallery Source in the filters section to select the source for the script content. Select PowerShell Gallery and click OK to use the PowerShell Gallery as the source. When you use the PowerShell Gallery as the source, you can search by using free text, or you can search by keyword : value . For example, you can use Tag: O365 to find any scripts tagged with Office 365. You can also use the filters to search by script type and by publisher.

title: General availability: Azure Site Recovery in new Azure experience
content: Azure Site Recovery , a component of Microsoft Operations Management Suite , is generally available in the new Azure experience. Those familiar with Site Recovery will be happy with the new look and feel, as well as these enhancements: Azure Resource Manager support for all scenarios First-class support for Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) subscriptions Enhanced VMware to Azure Support for Resource Manager deployments and classic deployments New exclude disk functionality in replicating VMware virtual machines to Azure Support for Azure Premium Storage for high-churn workloads System Center Virtual Machine Manager (VMM) to Azure Support for Resource Manager deployments and classic deployments Support for protecting multiple virtual machines at the same time Hyper-V site to Azure Support for Resource Manager deployments and classic deployments Support for protecting multiple virtual machines at the same time VMM to VMM through Hyper-V Replica Support for protecting multiple virtual machines at the same time Streamlined getting started experience for all Site Recovery scenarios New replication policy construct to enable flexible association and management Support for locally redundant storage as a target Functionality of Azure Backup and Site Recovery in a single "Recovery Services vault" construct

title: Azure Cosmos DB: General availability in the North Central region
content: Azure Cosmos DB now supports provisioning Cosmos DB accounts in the North Central US region. This brings the total region count to 18, including: Central US, East US, South Central US, West US, North Europe, West Europe, East Asia, Southeast Asia, both regions in Japan and Australia, all three regions in India, and both preview regions in Germany. The India regions are available to volume licensing customers and partners with a local enrollment in India. Try out Azure Cosmos DB today by signing up for a Microsoft Azure free account , and then create a Azure Cosmos DB database account by using the Azure portal . For more information about Azure Cosmos DB, visit the Azure Cosmos DB page .

title: Azure SQL Data Warehouse: May 2016 update
content: Several features have been added to Azure SQL Data Warehouse in our most recent update: ​ Azure Active Directory authentication Large-row support Transaction size limits Improved Visual Studio support Support for varchar(max) , nvarchar(max) , varbinary(max) , numeric , and uniqueidentifier data types Support for RAND() , CHECKSUM() , BINARY_CHECKSUM() , NEWID() , and IS_SRVROLEMEMBER() functions Support for the sys.database_service_objectives dynamic management view (DMV) for Azure SQL Data Warehouse databases Archival compression for clustered columnstore tables To learn more about these updates, see Azure SQL Data Warehouse now supports Azure Active Directory, large rows, and additional T-SQL features .

title: Scheduler available in Canada regions
content: Azure Scheduler is available in the Canada East and Canada Central regions. Canada is a Scheduler geo-region that is paired for high availability and ensures that data stays within Canada. For more information on Azure Scheduler, visit the service webpage .

title: Resource lock management available in the portal
content: Management locks help you prevent accidental deletion or modification of your Azure resources. You can manage these locks from within the Azure portal. To view, add, or delete locks, go to the RESOURCE MANAGEMENT section of any resource's settings blade. For more information, see the documentation for management locks .

title: Azure Data Lake update announcement
content: The Azure Data Lake engineering team has been working hard on refining the services, and a few recent updates provide basic improvements across the board. You can find detailed descriptions of all the updates in the following release notes: U-SQL Azure Data Lake Tools for Visual Studio Azure portal Among all those updates, there are a few things the team would like to draw your attention to: There's better compatibility with other tools when a U-SQL script sends output to Azure Storage blobs. The Azure SDK includes Azure Data Lake Tools for Visual Studio. This makes it easier than ever to get the tools you need from a single location. Both Azure Data Lake Store and Azure Data Lake Analytics support writing diagnostic logs. This is very useful if you need to perform auditing of how the services are being used. You can visit the Azure Data Lake blog for technical articles about Data Lake Store, Data Lake Analytics, and Azure HDInsight. If you have any suggestions or feedback, feel free to go to the feedback page and create an entry there. If you have any questions about using Data Lake, you can post it on the MSDN forum to get answers from the product team or the community.

title: General availability: Azure SQL Database elastic pools
content: Azure SQL Database elastic pools are ideally suited for SaaS and line-of-business applications that need the performance, availability, and security isolation benefits of provisioning one database for each tenant or application. Each elastic database in the pool gets the resources it needs when it needs them, which eliminates the complexity of managing individual database performance. Elastic pools provide the best price performance for a group of databases while delivering performance elasticity for each database. Elastic pool features include: Autoscaling you control: Pools automatically scale performance and storage capacity for elastic databases on the fly. You can control the performance assigned to a pool, add or remove elastic databases on demand, and define performance of elastic databases without affecting the overall cost of the pool. For more information, please visit the When should an elastic database pool be used? documentation page. Intelligent management of your environment: Built-in sizing recommendations proactively identify databases that would benefit from pools and allow “what-if” analysis for quick optimization to meet your performance goals. Rich performance monitoring and troubleshooting dashboards help you visualize historical pool utilization. For more information, please visit the Monitor and manage an elastic database pool with the Azure portal documentation page. Performance and price that meet your needs: Basic, Standard, and Premium pools offer a broad spectrum of performance, storage, and pricing options. Pools can contain up to 400 elastic databases. Elastic databases can autoscale up to 1,000 elastic database transaction units (eDTUs). Please note that in a few regions, elastic pools will remain in public preview for a limited time. For a list of these regions, please visit the SQL Database pricing page. For more information on elastic pools, please visit the What is an Azure elastic database pool? documentation page, the Azure blog , and the Elastic databases helps SaaS developers tame explosive growth video.

title: Public preview: Media Analytics for Azure Media Services
content: Media Analytics is a collection of speech and vision services that makes it easier for organizations and enterprises to derive actionable insights from their video files through advanced machine learning technology. Media Analytics services are hosted by the Azure Media Services platform, our cloud media solution for encoding, encrypting, and streaming audio or video at scale, live or on demand (VOD). Media Analytics is offered at enterprise scale, delivering the compliance, security, and global reach that large organizations need. For more information, please visit the Azure blog or the Media Analytics page.

title: Public preview: Speaker Recognition API for Microsoft Cognitive Services
content: Microsoft Cognitive Services is a collection of APIs that are available to developers to make their applications more intelligent and engaging. This set of services expands on our evolving portfolio of machine learning APIs and lets developers easily add intelligent features to their solutions. Speaker Recognition API is now in public preview. Its features include: Speaker verification , using voice for authentication. The API can be used to power applications with an intelligent verification tool. For example, if the speaker claims a certain identity, you can use their voice to verify this claim. Speaker identification , to recognize who is speaking. The API can be used to determine the identity of an unknown speaker. Input audio of the unknown speaker is compared to a group of selected speakers and if a match is found, the speaker’s identity is returned. Speaker Recognition API is available as a stand-alone service. Public preview pricing went into effect on May 2, 2016. For more information about pricing, please visit the Cognitive Services pricing page.

title: General availability: Azure in Canada
content: On May 10, 2016, Azure became generally available from datacenters in Toronto and Quebec City. Azure customers in Canada can now benefit from enterprise-grade reliability and performance combined with in-country data residency. This includes data replication in two locations within Canada for business continuity and the option of a private connection to the cloud with Azure ExpressRoute. For more information, please visit the Azure blog and the Azure regions page.

title: Test-drive feature is now available on Azure Marketplace
content: You can now try Azure Marketplace without an Azure subscription or making a payment. For example, if you want to experience Trend Micro’s Deep Security running on Azure , you can take a test drive first without the commitment. Launch a preconfigured image running on Azure with a couple of clicks, then explore, and finally decide whether it’s right for you. Several partners, including Trend Micro, are participating. For more information, please visit the Test drives on Microsoft Azure page.

title: General availability: Azure Content Delivery Network from Akamai is now available
content: Today we're excited to announce the general availability of Azure Content Delivery Network from Akamai. Akamai has more than 200,000 servers in 129 countries, which provides Azure customers an expanded global footprint and reach, particularly in Latin America and Asia. Ninety percent of the world's Internet users are within a single "network hop" of an Akamai content delivery network server. This provides a significant opportunity to accelerate applications that are built on Azure. With the integration of Akamai's industry-leading content delivery network capabilities directly into the Azure cloud platform, customers can instantly provision and go live within minutes. With this release, we're unveiling new pricing tiers: Azure Content Deilvery Network Standard from Verizon, Azure Content Deilvery Network Standard from Akamai, and Azure Content Deilvery Network Premium from Verizon. For more information about Azure Content Delivery Network products and features, see the overview .

title: API Management adds new cmdlets for managing Git configuration, Properties, and Loggers
content: With the release of Azure PowerShell 1.4.0, a number of new cmdlets were added to manage Tenant Git configuration, Properties, and Loggers in API Management. To check out the new cmdlets, see GitHub .

title: Announcing Azure Mobile Services transition to Azure App Service
content: This service announcement affects you only if you're running Azure Mobile Services. We're transitioning from Azure Mobile Services to Azure App Service. While no action is required on your part, please note that the management experience will change. You can choose to migrate before September 1, 2016 or wait until Azure migrates you. For more details on this topic and how to migrate your site, read the announcement blog post .

title: General availability: SQL Database Advisor and Performance dashboard
content: SQL Database Advisor and the Performance dashboard are now generally available in the Azure portal . Database Advisor helps you to improve the performance of your databases by providing intelligent tuning recommendations that are based on historical usage. Database Advisor replaces the former Index Advisor feature and brings two new types of recommendations: Initial release of FIX SCHEMA ISSUES recommendations (in preview) Initial release of PARAMETERIZE QUERIES recommendations (in preview) For more detailed information, check out the SQL Database Advisor and Performance dashboard articles.

title: Public preview: More preview enhancements for Azure Active Directory B2C
content: A set of new features has been added to Azure Active Directory B2C , which is currently in preview. The new features are: Support for Microsoft account as a social identity provider (Facebook, Google, LinkedIn, and Amazon were already supported). Unified sign-up or sign-in policy. Self-service password reset policy. Configurable token lifetimes, sessions, and single sign-on behavior. Easy access to Azure AD B2C features on the Azure portal. For more details, see More preview enhancements for Azure AD B2C .

title: Azure Cosmos DB: Expire data automatically with
content: Microsoft Azure Cosmos DB now provides the ability to set the length of time in which a document lives in the database before being automatically purged. This length of time is referred to as the document's "time-to-live" (TTL) and is measured in seconds since the document was last modified. You can set this value at the collection level and override it on a per-document basis. If a time-to-live value is set, Azure Cosmos DB automatically removes documents that exist after that period of time. For more information about time-to-live, see the Expire data in Azure Cosmos DB collections automatically with time to live ​ article or the Azure Cosmos DB now supports time to live blog post.

title: Azure Scheduler: P10 and new P20 Premium plans
content: The current Azure Scheduler Premium plan has been renamed to P10 Premium, and a new P20 Premium plan has been released. The new P20 Premium plan allows for applications that use large numbers of jobs to support 1000 jobs per job collection. To learn more about Scheduler pricing, see Scheduler pricing details .

title: Public preview: Windows 10 Enterprise State Roaming preview via Azure Active Directory Premium is now available in Asia
content: In Windows 10, Enterprise State Roaming brings the settings sync experience, which Microsoft account sign-in provides to consumers, to enterprise users. Through Azure Active Directory Join , users can use their organizational identities to roam their settings and modern app data using Azure cloud for storage. Enterprise users benefit from a unified experience across their Azure Active Directory–joined Windows 10 devices. They are also protected from modern app data loss due to hardware failure, theft, or device replacement. Enterprises benefit from enhanced security and better control of the enterprise data. All data is encrypted with Azure Rights Management before leaving the device. This capability is available only with an Azure Active Directory Premium subscription. Enterprise State Roaming preview for Windows 10 is now available in the East and Southeast Asia Azure regions.

title: Public preview: Azure Active Directory Domain Services now available in Australia
content: The public preview of Azure Active Directory Domain Services is now available in Azure’s Australia East and Australia Southeast regions.

title: General availability: Announcing support for PHP 7.0 in Azure App Service
content: PHP 7.0 is a major milestone in the PHP Community because it's a significant rewrite to the core of PHP to make the language run the same workloads faster—in many cases three times faster. There's a huge push in the community to update extensions, components, and frameworks to support PHP 7. Another exciting milestone with the PHP 7 release in Azure App Service is that this is the first time we're supporting an x64 runtime for PHP in our public cloud. This will expand our offering to a new set of customers who rely on x64 bits to handle their workloads. See the blog post with more details about this release.

title: Mid-June 2016 brings compatibility level 130 for new Azure SQL databases
content: Azure SQL Database runs millions of databases under several different T-SQL versions, preserving backward compatibility for applications. SQL Database implements a versioning technique called "compatibility level." The compatibility levels are: SQL Server 2008 and SQL Database v11: 100 SQL Server 2012: 110 SQL Server 2014 and SQL Database: 120 SQL Server 2016 and SQL Database v12: 130 Use of compatibility level 130 enables developers to benefit from SQL Server 2016 query processor enhancements. The enhancements can improve your query executions by leveraging new features such as parallel plan execution, serial batch mode execution, and new query plan estimates, to name a few. Starting in mid-June 2016 , the default Azure SQL Database compatibility level will change from 120 to 130 for newly created databases. Databases created before mid-June 2016 will not be affected and will maintain their current compatibility level (100, 110, or 120). For pre-existing databases, we strongly encourage you to adopt this new compatibility level so you can benefit from the new query processor features and increase your application performance. You can change the compatibility level by running a simple T-SQL statement: “ALTER DATABASE <Your-Database-Name-Here> SET COMPATIBILITY_LEVEL = 130”. Experience shows that most workloads run as-is under compatibility level 130. However, there are always some exceptions, and due diligence is important to determine how much you can benefit from the enhancements. If you want to dive deeper on this matter, you can review the documentation: Improved query performance with compatibility level 130 in Azure SQL Database .

title: Public preview: Platform-supported migration of IaaS resources
content: We're excited to announce the public preview of a new service for platform-supported migration of IaaS resources from the classic to the Azure Resource Manager stack. This service allows you to migrate your IaaS virtual machines (VMs) and network resources through a step-by-step-workflow from the classic to the Resource Manager stack. The two scopes that we're offering with this preview are migrating "VMs not in a virtual network" and a "virtual network along with all the VMs." This migration service is now available in all regions where virtual machines are available, and there is no additional cost. To learn more about how to get started, see the platform-supported migration documentation .

title: Azure API Management adds support for Swagger model schemas
content: We released a new feature to store model schemas from Swagger files and display model schemas in API documentation in the Azure portal.

title: Public preview: Azure Search Blob indexer parses structured JSON content
content: Azure Search indexers for Blob storage were announced in March with the ability to crack open and index major document formats, including PDF, Microsoft Office, HTML, JSON, and more. The Blob storage indexer can now parse JSON blobs and select any part of the JSON payload for indexing in Azure Search. Currently, this functionality is in preview. It is available only in the REST API version 2015-02-28-Preview. Read this article to learn more!

title: Mobile Apps iOS Client SDK v3.1.0 released
content: We released an update to the iOS Client SDK for the Mobile Apps feature of Azure App Service. This update contains a fix to Azure Active Directory authentication and switches the SDK to use WebKit instead of WebView. For more information, see the change log and the documentation .

title: Active geo-replication available on all Azure SQL Database service tiers
content: Effective immediately, we’ve expanded our geo-replication features by enabling Active geo-replication across Azure SQL Database Basic and Standard service tiers. As a result, Standard geo-replication will be retired in April 2017. By using Active geo-replication in either a Basic database or a Standard database, customers receive numerous benefits that deliver greater security and business continuity in disaster situations: Database-level disaster recovery goes quickly when you’ve replicated transactions to databases on different SQL Database servers in the same or different regions. Cross-region redundancy allows applications to recover from permanent loss of a datacenter caused by natural disasters, catastrophic human errors, or malicious acts. Online secondary databases are readable, and they can be used as load balancers for read-only workloads such as reporting. With automatic asynchronous replication, after an online secondary database has been seeded, updates to the primary database are automatically copied to the secondary database. For more information about Active geo-replication and its full set of capabilities, please visit the Active geo-replication for Azure SQL Database documentation page. For more information about pricing, please visit the SQL Database pricing page.

title: Azure IoT Gateway SDK enters public beta
content: The Azure IoT Gateway SDK enters public beta today. It facilitates the creation of on-premises gateways that allow your IoT solution to do more: connect purpose-built and legacy devices without replacing existing infrastructure, run analytics on the edge, perform time-sensitive decisions by minimizing latency, and enforce security and privacy constraints. We invite you to check it out on GitHub ! Inside the repo, you will find documentation to get you started with the SDK, and samples to get your own gateway up and running in no time.

title: New Dv2 instances for Azure HDInsight
content: We’re announcing a new instance size, D5 v2, that extends the Dv2-Series for Azure HDInsight. D5 v2 has 16 cores and 56 GB of memory. Dv2-Series nodes are currently available in Australia East, Australia Southeast, West US, East US, East US 2, South Central US, North Central US, Central US, North Europe, West Europe, East Asia, Southeast Asia, and Japan East. For more information, please visit the HDInsight and HDInsight pricing pages.

content: Azure DevTest Labs is live in all 15 public regions that support the required Azure resources used in the Labs — including Australia, Brazil, and more regions in the United States, Europe, and Asia: NEW - Brazil South NEW - Australia East NEW - Australia Southeast NEW - North Central US NEW - North Europe NEW - Southeast Asia Central US East US East US 2 South Central US West US West Europe East Asia Japan East Japan West Customers now have the option to create a DevTest lab in any of these locations. Azure DevTest Labs is a service that helps developers and testers quickly create environments in Azure while minimizing waste and controlling cost. You can test the latest version of your application by provisioning Windows and Linux environments through reusable templates and artifacts. Easily integrate your deployment pipeline with DevTest Labs to provision on-demand environments. Scale up your load testing by provisioning multiple test agents, and create pre-provisioned environments for training and demos. Please try it today and let us know what you think about it! If you have an idea for how to make it work better, submit your feedback (or vote for others) at the Azure DevTest Labs feedback forum . Have a question? title: General availability: Azure Cool Blob storage
content: Cool Blob storage is now generally available . Cool storage is low-cost storage for object data that is infrequently accessed and long lived​. Example use cases include backups, media content, scientific data, compliance data, and archival data. In general, any data that lives for a longer period of time and is accessed less than once a month is a candidate for Cool storage. With the new Blob storage accounts, you can choose between Hot and Cool access tiers to store object data based on its access pattern. Capabilities of Blob storage accounts include: Cost effectiveness : You can now store your less frequently accessed data in the Cool access tier at a low storage cost (as low as $0.01 per gigabyte in some regions), and your more frequently accessed data in the Hot access tier at a lower access cost. For more details on regional pricing, see the​ Azure Storage pricing page. Compatibility : We have designed Blob storage accounts to be 100 percent API compatible with our existing Blob storage offering, so you can make use of the new storage accounts in existing applications seamlessly. Performance : Data in the Cool access tier and data in the Hot access tier have a similar performance profile in terms of latency and throughput. Availability : The Hot access tier guarantees a high availability of 99.9 percent, whereas the Cool access tier offers a slightly lower availability of 99 percent. With the RA-GRS redundancy option , we provide a higher read SLA of 99.99 percent for the Hot access tier and 99.9 percent for the Cool access tier. Durability : Both access tiers provide the same high durability that you have come to expect from Azure Storage and the same data replication options that you use today. Scalability and Security : Blob storage accounts provide the same scalability and security features as our existing offering. Global reach : Blob storage accounts are available for use starting today in most Azure regions. You can find the updated list of available regions on the Azure services by region page. For more details on how to start using this feature, please see our getting-started documentation .

title: Azure IoT Suite goes international
content: We are expanding the regional availability of Azure IoT Suite to include Australia and Japan, as well as Microsoft Azure Deutschland (preview), a Microsoft cloud with German data trustee T-Systems. The IoT Suite provisioning sites ( https://www.azureiotsuite.com and https://www.azureiotsuite.de ), along with both preconfigured solutions, support German, Japanese, and 14 other languages. For more information, take a look at the Remote Monitoring v1.3.0 release notes and the Predictive Maintenance v1.1.0 release notes .

title: Azure Stream Analytics integration with Power BI is now generally available
content: Itegration between Azure Stream Analytics and Power BI is now generally availabile. This integration enables you to output data directly from your streaming jobs to a real-time dashboards built in Power BI. Real-time dashboards are a core scenario in streaming as they allow you to gain low latency insights in to your data in-motion which would otherwise be impossible. With this integration between Stream Analytics and Power BI, building such dashboards is simple and intuitive. For more information on this release, please see the following blog announcement - https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/streamanalytics-and-powerbi/

title: Public preview: Microsoft Cognitive Services
content: Microsoft Cognitive Services is a collection of APIs available to developers to make their applications more intelligent and engaging. This set of services expands on our evolving portfolio of machine learning APIs and lets developers easily add intelligent features—such as vision, speech, language, and knowledge capabilities—to their solutions. The following services are now in public preview so developers can deploy the most advanced AI algorithms by using simple, RESTful APIs: Face and Emotion APIs , which can analyze and deeply understand image content. The algorithms can detect people and provide approximate personal attributes such as age, gender, and emotion. Speech API , to support speech recognition (speech to text) and synthesis (text to speech). Language APIs , for understanding the context within a text segment: Web Language Model API offers advanced natural language processing, such as word breaking and auto completion. Text Analytics API provides sentiment analysis and key phrase extraction. Language Understanding Intelligent Service API helps applications process natural language commands in a matter of minutes. Recommendations API , for helping to predict which items of a catalog are more likely to be of interest to customers. Microsoft Cognitive Services APIs are available as stand-alone services, and public preview pricing will go into effect on April 1, 2016. For more information about pricing, please visit the Cognitive Services pricing page.

title: Azure HDInsight supports R for machine learning and new updates to Spark and Hadoop
content: We’ve made major investments in Azure HDInsight , the managed Hadoop-as-a-service offering from Microsoft. HDInsight can run 100 percent open-source R to do machine learning and has new updates on the latest Hadoop and Spark components from Hortonworks: R Server for HDInsight in Azure Data Lake provides the only 100 percent managed and scalable R solution in the cloud. This makes it easy for data scientists to use their most popular programming language for predictive modeling and machine learning to scale their analysis over any size of data by using Hadoop and Spark clusters in HDInsight. Spark for HDInsight in Data Lake , previously announced as a public preview, is available on the latest Apache Spark 1.6 edition. This greatly improves performance and introduces new data science functionality. With Spark for HDInsight, we offer customers a fully managed, enterprise-ready solution with a choice of compelling, interactive user experiences. HDInsight is available on Hortonworks Data Platform 2.4 , giving customers the latest and greatest from the Apache Hadoop ecosystem. R Server is part of a new premium offering in HDInsight. For more information about pricing, please visit the HDInsight pricing page.

title: Public preview: Azure Storage Service Encryption
content: Azure Storage Service Encryption is now available for Azure Blob Storage (block and page blobs) upon request for any new storage account created through Azure Resource Manager. Accounts enabled with this feature encrypt data with Microsoft-managed keys by using the industry-leading 256-bit Advanced Encryption Standard (AES-256) algorithm. This is a fully managed encryption process: Microsoft performs key management, rotation, and compliance with key standards. Customers with security and compliance requirements can take advantage of this feature now. For more information, please visit the Storage security guide and Storage Service Encryption documentation pages. For more information about pricing, please visit the Azure Storage pricing page.

title: General availability: Azure Data Catalog
content: Azure Data Catalog is an enterprise-wide metadata catalog that stores, describes, indexes, and shows how to access any registered data asset. It makes data source discovery easy and facilitates collaboration between those who seek information and those who create it. In contrast to traditional metadata management solutions that focus on IT, Data Catalog bridges the gap between IT and business users. It allows users with knowledge of the data to enrich the system by annotating each data asset as it is discovered. And IT can still maintain control and oversight as the system evolves by locking down visibility to selected assets as the need occurs. For more information about its capabilities, please visit the Data Catalog documentation page. Data Catalog is offered in both Free and Standard editions, and general availability pricing will be in effect starting May 1, 2016. For more information about pricing, please visit the Data Catalog pricing page.

title: Azure Cosmos DB: New pricing option
content: We are excited to announce a new pricing option for Azure Cosmos DB, offering greater flexibility in optimizing cost and performance. You can use the new pricing option to reserve throughput independently from data storage for a collection. You have the flexibility to incrementally adjust throughput for a collection over time as needed. Throughput is billed on the amount reserved, whereas SSD-backed storage can be billed on the amount consumed. To learn more about Azure Cosmos DB pricing, see Azure Cosmos DB pricing details .

title: Azure Managed Cache Service and Azure In-Role Cache to be retired November 30, 2016
content: This is a follow-up reminder to our announcement last year regarding the retirement plan. Azure Managed Cache Service and the Azure In-Role Cache service will remain available for existing customers until November 30, 2016. After this date, Managed Cache Service will be shut down, and the In-Role Cache service will no longer be supported. We’ll remove support for creating new in-role caches in the first Azure SDK release that happens after February 1, 2016. Customers will be able to open existing projects that have in-role caches.

title: General availability: Azure Service Fabric
content: The Azure Service Fabric SDK for Windows and the Service Fabric Azure-hosted service have reached general availability (GA). Service Fabric is now generally available for deployment to Windows Server virtual machines running in Azure. This means that you can confidently deploy production workloads and that subsequent releases will offer backward compatibility. For more information, visit the Service Fabric documentation page.

title: Public preview: Service Fabric for Windows Server
content: Today, we are beginning the public preview for our stand-alone Windows Server package. You can use this package to create a multi-machine Azure Service Fabric cluster in your own datacenter or in other public clouds—in effect, anywhere that you can create network connectivity between physical or virtual machines. After you have set up one of these stand-alone clusters, it will work just like one that you might have deployed in Azure. You can deploy the same app packages and even publish directly from Visual Studio. Read more about the Service Fabric for Windows Server preview .

title: Private preview of Service Fabric on Linux
content: We are committed to enabling you to use Azure Service Fabric however and wherever you like. Today, we are taking another major step in that direction by opening a private preview of Service Fabric on Linux, including Java language support for stateless and actor services. In addition to running internally for many years, the Service Fabric private preview program has been operating with customers for more than a year. More than 300 customers have used it to build applications and services. To learn more about our plans for Linux and to sign up to be considered for the preview, see Service Fabric on Linux .

title: Azure Cosmos DB: Partitioned collections for higher storage and throughput
content: The latest Azure Cosmos DB service update includes support to create partitioned collections , which can support larger data volumes and process more requests. Partitioned collections support up to 250 GB of storage and 250,000 request units per second of provisioned throughput. (You can increase both limits by filing a support ticket .) You can create partitioned collections via the Azure portal, REST API version 2015-12-16, and SDK versions 1.6.0 and newer in .NET, Node.js, Java, and Python. The programming model introduces partition keys during collection creation and as an argument for read, write, query, and execute stored-procedure operations on documents. Create a partitioned collection via the portal To learn more, you can: Review the documentation Partitioning and scaling in Azure Cosmos DB and Performance levels . Download the .NET , Node.js , Java , or Python SDK, or use the REST API version 2015-12-16 .

title: Public preview: Azure Cosmos DB protocol support for MongoDB
content: We are excited to announce the public preview of Azure Cosmos DB protocol support for MongoDB. Through this preview functionality, applications can easily and transparently communicate with Azure Cosmos DB by using existing, community-supported Apache license drivers for MongoDB. Developers can use their current tools and skills for MongoDB to build applications that take advantage of Azure Cosmos DB, a fully managed and scalable NoSQL database service backed by industry-leading SLAs. To learn how to request access to the preview by using the Azure portal, see the related Azure article .

title: General availability: Virtual Machine Scale Sets
content: We are excited to announce the general availability of Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets. VM Scale Sets are a new compute service that makes it very easy to deploy a large number of identically configured virtual machines together, and to integrate them with Azure Autoscale and Azure Load Balancer. VM Scale Sets are available in all regions where virtual machines are available, and they have no additional cost. Please give them a try today. To learn more, see the VM Scale Sets webpage .

title: Azure DevTest Labs: Monthly Estimated Cost Trend chart
content: Are you worried about the cost of your lab? Do you want to track the lab cost for the current month? Your wait is over, and now you can live in peace! Today, we are releasing a Monthly Estimated Cost Trend chart, part of our longer roadmap of enabling cost thresholds in the lab. You can enable the chart by going to the Cost thresholds policy under the lab settings. It can take up to 24 hours before you can see the cost. FAQs What is not included in the cost calculation? Your offer rates . Currently, we are not able to use your offer rates (shown under your subscription) that you have negotiated with Microsoft or Microsoft partners. We are using Pay-As-You-Go rates. Your taxes Your discounts Your billing currency . Currently, we are showing the lab cost in USD currency. Is there any time lag in reporting the cost? Typically, 90–95 percent of the cost is reported in 24 hours. But in cases of live site issues, outages, and other reasons, it can take more than 24 hours to report the cost. What is the data refresh interval? Currently, data is refreshed every 24 hours. Please try it today and let us know what you think about it! If you have an idea for how to make it work better, submit your feedback (or vote for others) at the Azure DevTest Labs feedback forum . Have a question? Check out answers or ask a new question at the MSDN Community forum .

title: Microsoft Azure IoT reference architecture available
content: The Microsoft Azure IoT reference architecture is available as a PDF download . The reference architecture provides guidance for building secure and scalable, device-centric solutions for connecting devices, conducting analysis, and integrating with back-end systems.

title: Update: Automation Hybrid Worker
content: An update to Azure Automation Hybrid Worker has just been released. You can verify that the latest version has been applied to your Microsoft Monitoring Agent installation by confirming that the following subfolder matches this version number: %ProgramFiles%\Microsoft Monitoring Agent\Agent\AzureAutomation\7.2.7396.0. This version includes the following improvements: Reliability fixes Ability to work with the “Windows PowerShell\Turn on Script Execution” policy enabled Pre-check for proxy setting during worker registration, with a clear error message when it fails the check Support for running graphical runbooks, consistent with running them directly in Azure For the update to be successfully installed, you need to restart the Microsoft Monitoring Agent service.

title: Public preview: JSON in Azure SQL Database
content: JSON functionalities are available in Azure SQL Database V12 (preview). You can use new JSON functionalities to integrate Azure SQL Database with other services that exchange data in the JSON format. With the new JSON functionalities, you can: Read data from JSON text by using JSON_VALUE/JSON_QUERY functions. Modify JSON text by using the JSON_MODIFY function. Transform JSON text into a relational format by using the OPENJSON function - OPENJSON function requires database COMPATIBILITY_LEVEL = 130! Easily query or import JSON data into tables. Query relational and JSON data stored in any relational table. Format the results of SQL queries as JSON text and send it to any service or framework that uses JSON (for example, JavaScript/jQuery components and AngularJS/ReactJS frameworks). You don't need any special setup to start using JSON. If you have apps that are sending JSON text to SQL Server or if you use JSON text that is already stored in your tables, simply write a query that gets the values from your JSON documents. For more information, see our official documentation and blog posts .

title: Announcing: New Dv2-series virtual machine size
content: A larger virtual machine size has joined the Dv2-series. This new size is the Standard_D15_v2 with the following specifications: 20 CPU cores, 140 GB of memory, 1,000 GB of temporary solid-state drive (SSD), up to 8 virtual network interface cards (NICs), up to 40 data disks, and very high network bandwidth. Each Standard_D15_v2 instance is isolated to hardware dedicated to a single customer, to provide a high degree of isolation from other customers. This addition and the Standard_G5 are the two available sizes that are on hardware dedicated to a single customer. The Standard_D15_v2 is available in all locations that support the Dv2-series, as described on the Azure services by region page. This size is available for virtual machines that use the Azure Resource Manager deployment model and custom OS images published by Canonical, CoreOS, OpenLogic, Oracle, Puppet Labs, Red Hat, SUSE, and Microsoft.

title: Azure IoT Hub client SDK portable libraries are available on NuGet
content: We have a PCL package available on NuGet.org. The PCL library supports Android, iOS, Windows 10 (UWP) and Windows Phone (WinRT). Android and iOS support was made possible thanks to Xamarin. This initial release enables the client to run over HTTP.

title: Azure compliance: Azure Cosmos DB certified for ISO 27001, HIPAA, and the EU Model Clauses
content: The Azure Cosmos DB team is excited to announce that Azure Cosmos DB is ISO 27001 , HIPAA , and EU Model Clauses compliant. ISO 27001 is a security standard that is intended to bring information security under explicit management control. It is one of the most widely recognized certifications for a cloud service. We are proud to join the family of Microsoft cloud services in scope for ISO/IEC 27001. Along with ISO 27001, Azure Cosmos DB is certified for HIPAA and the EU Model Clauses. HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) establishes requirements for the use, disclosure, and safeguarding of individually identifiable health information. The EU (European Union) Model Clauses help ensure that any personal data that leaves the EEA (European Economic Area) is transferred in compliance with EU data-protection law. With these certifications and attestations, we hope to unlock new business opportunities for customers to adopt Azure Cosmos DB. From this milestone, we will continue to meet and attain key international and industry-specific compliance standards.

content: This post summarizes the new features released in Azure SQL Data Warehouse in February 2016: T-SQL Implemented new T-SQL needed for SQL Server Management Studio integration. Loading Improved PolyBase, enabling loads from public data sets. Restore Added the ability to restore SQL Data Warehouse backups to any server in any region. Monitoring Integrated views of Data Warehouse Unit consumption for the current workload. Documentation Released a broad set of documentation additions and changes. content: The Azure API Management Ingest Tool gives Visual Studio developers a one-click way to place REST APIs behind an Azure API Management instance. With API Management, you can manage, throttle, and understand the usage of your API endpoints. For more information and to get started, see Azure API Management Publishing Tool . title: Azure DevTest Labs: Create custom images from a lab VM
content: Azure DevTest Labs becomes an even better place for you to prepare and create your VM images (VHDs) today. After you provision and verify a VM in DevTest Labs, you can click the ellipsis (...) for that particular VM and choose Create custom image . The created custom images are stored in the "generatedvhds" blob container of the lab's storage account, and they're available as a VM base for all the lab users to create VMs. In addition, you can choose to use sysprep (or not) for a Windows VM. Figure 1: Create custom image command Figure 2: Create custom image blade Through the Azure portal, you can also do that from an Azure Resource Manager template. Here are the quick-start templates that demonstrate how to create custom images from both Windows and Linux lab VMs: Create a custom image from a Windows lab VM Create a custom image from a Linux lab VM Please try it today and let us know what you think about it! title: Update: Automation Graphical Authoring SDK
content: An update to the public preview of the Microsoft Azure Automation Graphical Authoring SDK has been released. The update addresses some compatibility issues. Go to Microsoft Azure Automation Graphical Authoring SDK to download the latest version.

title: Compliance updates for Azure public cloud
content: We’re adding more certification coverage to our Azure portfolio, so regulated customers can take advantage of new services: Microsoft has renewed our Azure Service Organization Controls (SOC) 1 and 2 Reports, expanding service coverage to include 14 new services in SOC, and achieved a SOC 3. New Azure in-scope services include: Scheduler, API Management, Azure Redis Cache, ExpressRoute, Automation, Load Balancer, HDInsight, Premium Storage, SQL Database, Event Hubs, Sync Fabric (Microsoft Azure Active Directory [Azure AD]), Password Single Sign-on (Azure AD), Self-Service Group Management (Azure AD), and Operational Insights. Microsoft renewed our Azure Payment Card Industry (PCI) certification, updating PCI Data Security Standard (DSS) 3.0 to PCI DSS 3.1 and expanding service coverage. Services added with this certification include HDInsight, Key Vault, Azure Resource Manager, and Azure Redis Cache. Microsoft has achieved Japan Cloud Security Gold Mark (CS Gold Mark) accreditation by Japan Information Security Audit Association (JASA). The scope includes all layers (IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS) with Azure and Office 365 and all regions operated by Microsoft that have achieved SOC 2 Type 2. CS Gold Mark is a standard based on ISO/IEC 27017. For more information, please visit the Compliance , SOC 1, 2, and 3 Reports , Payment Card Industry (PCI) Data Security Standard (DSS) Level 1 , and Cloud Security Mark (Gold) pages.

title: Automation: Activity output object properties exposed to simplify graphical runbook authoring
content: When you author graphical runbooks in Azure Automation, a common pattern is to use the output of one activity as the input to a later activity. Previously, the UX allowed selection only of the entire output object. Any properties of the object needed to be discovered independently and entered manually. Now the UX exposes the property hierarchy of the activity output objects so that you can choose to use a selected object property as input to an activity. This is a big time saver when you're authoring graphical runbooks. Currently, the properties are exposed for cmdlets that have the OutputType attribute set. To learn more about setting OutputType in your PowerShell cmdlets so that they can be used easily in graphical runbooks, refer to the about_Functions_OutputTypeAttribute article and the OutputType Attribute Declaration article. Activity output object properties

title: Use API Management properties to manage secrets and global values in API Management policies
content: With the release of Azure API Management properties, each API Management service instance has a properties collection of key/value pairs that are global to that service instance. You can use these properties to manage constant string values, including secrets, across all API configuration and policies. Properties can contain literal strings, policy expressions, and secrets. They can be used in API Management policies as complete or partial element and attribute values. You can use properties to: Store any secrets that are used in policies outside the policy statements themselves. Store attribute values that are used in more than one policy and can be changed in one place if needed. To get started using properties, see How to use properties in Azure API Management policies .

title: Azure DevTest Labs: Use Azure Marketplace images to create VMs in the lab
content: You can manage and use Azure Marketplace images in Azure DevTest Labs to create lab VMs, as long as the Marketplace images meet the following criteria: The images create a single VM. The images use Azure Resource Manager to provision VMs. The images don't require purchasing an extra licensing plan. You can update the lab settings to allow all qualified Azure Marketplace images in the lab or just some of them. Allow all qualified Azure Marketplace images in the lab or select some of the images When No is selected for Allow all Azure Marketplace images as VM bases , you can select the images that you want to allow in the lab, or you can select nothing so that none of the Azure Marketplace images can be used in the lab. Allowed Azure Marketplace images appear in the same list of VM bases with custom images when you create a lab VM. Select an Azure Marketplace image as the base to create a lab VM Please try it today and let us know what you think about it! If you have an idea for how to make it work better for you, submit your feedback (or vote for others) at the Azure DevTest Labs feedback forum . Have a question?
