title: Azure Websites: Scalable CMS with WordPress is now in the App Gallery!
content: To help enterprises set up robust CMS-backed sites, we are introducing a scalable WordPress offering available in the application gallery. With Scalable WordPress, new sites are automatically configured to leverage Azure capabilities such as Azure Storage for media assets, optimize performance with curated WordPress plugins, and provide a scalable back end with Standard Websites instances and higher end MySQL SKUs. Learn More Learn more about how to host a Scalable CMS with Wordpress .

title: Azure Websites with CDN Support
content: The Azure Content Delivery Network (CDN) is a service that allows you to send audio, images, and other static files faster and more reliably to customers across the globe. With a CDN, enterprises can save on compute costs while increasing site performance for their end users. This is especially critical for media-heavy corporate presence and marketing campaign sites. With the new CDN integration, users can now seamlessly integrate their site content with the Azure CDN using the Azure Management Portal. Learn More Learn more about CDN Integration with Websites .

title: Azure Websites: Now with Virtual Network Integration
content: Azure Websites VNET integration feature allows customers to securely connect to on-premises resources or other virtual machines hosted in Azure using a VPN connection, making Azure Websites an ideal solution for running both internal and external-facing applications. VNET integration is available as part of the Standard SKU. Paired with the Hybrid Connections feature, Azure Websites now provide customers with the flexibility to choose the right connectivity option to suit their application and enterprise network topology. Learn More Learn more about how to use Virtual Network Integration with Azure Websites .

title: Azure Site Recovery—simplified setup and supercharged with Azure Automation integration
content: Get started more easily with Azure Site Recovery and take advantage of integrated Azure Automation: Disaster Recovery Workflows are now supercharged. For recovery into Azure, create scripts using your Azure Automation subscription and call those scripts during your disaster-recovery drill or failover using the new Recovery Plan that is integrated with Azure Automation. Also, a new experience lets you monitor the progress of your Initial Replication to Azure after you start protecting your virtual machine to Azure. Azure Site Recovery has a greatly simplified setup experience to help you get started more easily—no more manual creation of certificates or pairing the certificates. Just download the vault credentials and use those during setup. It is as secure as before, yet much simpler than before. Check out Azure Site Recovery .

title: General Availability: Azure API Management
content: API Management , the service that launched in public preview on May 12, 2014, is generally available. The Azure API Management REST API Reference automates API management operations and integrates API management with other services. Use Delegation to control user sign-in, sign-up, and product subscription management operations. Updates to the Developer Portal (via OAuth-enabled APIs) include support for voice recognition and the addition of 10 new languages: English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, and Chinese. We also enabled full backup and restore of API Management services, improving disaster recovery and business continuity options for our customers. For more information, visit the API Management webpage . For a comprehensive look at pricing, visit the API Management Pricing Details webpage.

title: Role-based access control in Azure Preview portal
content: We've added support for role-based access control in the Azure Preview portal to help organizations meet their access management requirements simply and precisely. Now you can give Azure Active Directory users and groups access to the Azure resources they need to do their jobs, while not granting more access than they need. In this release, we’ve added these access management features: Group-based role assignment: You can assign access to Azure AD groups that can be synced from your local Active Directory. This enables you to leverage the existing investments that your organization has made in tooling and processes for managing groups. You can also use the delegated group management feature of Azure AD Premium . Three new roles: You can use three new roles—Owner, Contributor, and Reader—to ensure that users and groups have permission to do only the tasks they need to do their jobs. We’ll add support for custom roles in a future release. Service administrators and subscription coadministrators are automatically Owners in the Azure Preview portal. Granular access to resources: You can assign roles to users and groups for a particular subscription, resource group, or an individual Azure resource such as a website or database. In this way, you can ensure that users have access to all the resources they need and no access to resources that they do not need to manage. These features are available in the Azure Preview portal, Azure PowerShell, or from a custom client that uses the Azure Resource Management API. Access to the full Azure portal remains unchanged: only service administrators and coadministrators can access resources in that portal. Read our documentation to learn more about Role-Based Access Control in the Azure Preview Portal .

title: General Availability: Azure SQL Database Basic, Standard, and Premium service tiers
content: Three new Azure SQL Database service tiers—Basic, Standard, and Premium—are generally available. The tiers target seven performance levels, so they're flexible enough for light to heavyweight workloads. You can look forward to: 99.99 percent uptime SLA*, one of the highest for Azure services. Hourly billing for greater flexibility and budget management. Reduced prices (up to 50 percent from previously published generally available pricing). Or, choose our new Standard performance level for a cost-effective solution that falls between Basic and S1. All general availability pricing for Basic, Standard, and Premium tiers will take effect on November 1, 2014. Basic Standard Premium Uptime SLA Now increased to 99.99%* Database size limit 2 GB 250 GB 500 GB Self-service restore Any point within 7 days Any point within 14 days Any point within 35 days Disaster recovery Geo-restore to alternate Azure region Standard geo-replication, standby secondary Active geo-replication, up to 4 readable secondaries Performance objectives Transaction rate per hour Transaction rate per minute Transaction rate per second *99.99 percent uptime SLA does not apply to SQL Database Web and Business editions, which are supported at 99.9 percent. Basic: Designed for applications with a light transactional workload. Performance objectives for Basic provide a predictable hourly transaction rate. Standard: Designed as the go-to option for getting started with cloud-designed business applications. It offers mid-level performance and business continuity features. Performance objectives for Standard deliver predictable per-minute transaction rates. Premium: Designed for mission-critical databases, offers the highest performance levels and access to advanced business continuity features. Performance objectives for Premium deliver predictable per-second transaction rates. For more information on the new service tiers, please visit the Microsoft Azure Blog , and the SQL Database Pricing Details and Azure SQL Database Service Tiers (Editions) webpages.

title: General Availability: Internal Load Balancing
content: Internal load balancing (ILB) is now generally available. Starting today cloud services using Internal load balanced endpoints is subject to the same service-level agreement coverage that is offered in Azure. With Internal load balancing, customers can host their middle tier or backend applications behind a private IP address that is visible only within their cloud service or Virtual Network. Great examples of such applications are corpnet facing internal SharePoint sites, Virtual machines running SQL databases, and middle tier applications running core business logic. Internal load balanced endpoints can be used in isolation or along with public load balanced endpoints in the same cloud service. Visit the MSDN page or the blog post from May for detailed scenario descriptions and usage instructions.

title: Web Deploy as site extension for Azure Web Sites
content: We've created a new Web Deploy endpoint that lives as a site extension on your site. Using Web Deploy lets you host your own instance of the service, and lets us update it more frequently.

title: New enhancements to HDInsight
content: We've made the following updates to HDInsight service with our 6/24/2014 release: HDInsight 3.1 (HDP 2.1) is now generally available and is the default version for new clusters. HBase clusters, which are available in preview, can now be created in just 3 clicks from Azure Management Portal. Apache Mahout is now pre-installed on HDInsight 3.1 clusters. Hive queries can use Tez in HDInsight 3.1 to gain substantial performance improvements. Check out the HDInsight release notes for more information.

title: Traffic Manager support for weighted traffic distribution
content: Azure Traffic Manager’s round robin load-balancing method now supports weights. Combine this with support for external endpoints and explore a ton of new scenarios, including distributing traffic in hybrid scenarios between on-premises and the cloud. This feature is available via our APIs and PowerShell. For more information, check out the blog post .

title: Scheduler Premium tier and updates to Standard tier
content: Check out two new updates for Azure Scheduler : Scalable Standard tier. Scale up to 10 Standard units, and create up to 100 job collections (10 job collections per unit). New Premium tier. Receive 10,000 job collections per month with every Premium unit. For more information, please visit the Scheduler page. To get a comprehensive look at the pricing, visit the Scheduler Pricing Details page.

title: Microsoft Azure Site Recovery: Virtual Machines replication directly to Azure
content: Replicate virtual machines from your primary site directly to Azure (instead of to your own secondary site) with Azure Hyper-V Recovery Manager. In the event of an outage at the primary site, the service orchestrates the recovery of virtual machines in Azure. To better reflect the service’s new, broader capabilities, we're using this preview to give it a better name: "Microsoft Azure Site Recovery." The Azure Management Portal will be changing slightly to reflect the new name. If you want to continue replicating between two of your own sites, you don't need to do anything. If you want to start replicating to Azure, you'll need to create a new recovery plan. During preview the service is available at a 50 percent discount. For more information, please visit the Azure Site Recovery page. To get a comprehensive look at the pricing, please visit the Azure Site Recovery Pricing Detail s page.

title: New and improved Azure Service Health dashboard
content: We are are introducing a new and improved Azure Status dashboard at status.azure.com . With the new health dashboard you are able to personalize the dashboard to display the services and regions that you care about, and subscribe to RSS feeds for all services or only those that interest you.

title: Azure Web Sites supports Python 3.4
content: Azure Websites now supports Python 3.4, along with automatic configuration in the Azure Portal. Python is off by default, but when a specific Python version is selected a handler mapping is automatically generated and applied. Custom handler mappings (described in Azure Websites Python configuration documentation) are still supported.

title: Azure Websites Extensions
content: The latest release of Azure Web Sites includes a new gallery of website extensions for Azure. Use extensible management end points to leverage a powerful set of tools, like Visual Studio Online and management tools for connected resources like MySQL databases. Use the existing site extensions in the Azure Preview Portal, or create new ones and share them using the Site Extension Gallery submission portal (https://www.siteextensions.net).

title: Azure PowerShell 0.8.3
content: This Azure PowerShell release includes: A restructured source code and installation folder Web Sites: Return instances info from Get-AzureWebsite, and new "Slot1" and "Slot2" parameters for easier swapping between slots Traffic Manager: Support for Weighted Round Robin policies and Performance policies with external endpoints Role sizes information for Get-AzureRoleSize, Get-AzureAffinityGroup, Get-AzureService, and Get-AzureLocation cmdlets A new "ClusterType" parameter for HDInsight

title: Preview: HBase clusters in the HDInsight Service
content: HBase is a low-latency, NoSQL database designed for online transactional processing of big data. It's integrated into Azure as a managed cluster, and configured to use Azure Blob storage (which means you get low latency and flexibility when it comes to performance and cost). Build interactive websites that work with large datasets, or services that store sensor and telemetry data from millions of end points. Analyze your data using Hadoop jobs. HBase clusters are based on a Hortonworks distribution of Hadoop, and are compatible with existing HBase workloads and ecosystem components. For more information, see Get started using HBase with Hadoop in HDInsight .

title: General Availability: Brazil South region
content: The Azure Brazil South region (located in São Paulo state) is generally available, starting today. Host your services in Brazil South with the same service-level agreement coverage that we offer in Azure regions worldwide. Brazilian customers get better performance through reduced latency, and can keep Customer Storage Data in-country by choosing Locally Redundant Storage (note that the default - and most secure - storage option remains Geographically Redundant Storage ,which replicates data from Brazil South to our US South Central region). Visit the Azure website for detailed information on service availability and pricing . You can find more information about Brazil South general availability in the Microsoft Azure Blog .

title: SAP applications certified on Azure
content: Azure is now certified for SAP products, including SAP Business Suite, SAP NetWeaver, and SAP HANA Developer Edition. This means your business can deploy these solutions using Azure's reliable and secure cloud infrastructure platform. You'll have full support from Microsoft and SAP, including access to the SAP Cloud Appliance Library tool . Use your existing SAP licenses to deploy SAP software on Azure. Standard purchase models, pricing, and terms apply for Azure services. Check out SAP on Azure to learn more.

title: Azure Virtual Machines are available in US South Central and North Central regions
content: Azure Virtual Machines are an on-demand, scalable computing solution for your business. Create your own custom VM (or choose an image from the gallery), and deploy using Windows or Linux. Virtual machines only exist when you need them, saving money on infrastructure investments and software. The US South Central region is located in Texas, and the North Central region is in Illinois. Both regions will offer our Standard and recently introduced Basic compute tiers, along with Memory Intensive instances. Visit the Azure website for detailed information on service availability and VM pricing for both regions.

title: New region for Azure Websites: South Central US
content: The South Central US region (located in Texas) is now one of 4 regions in the United States (and 11 regions worldwide) supported by Azure Websites.

title: Azure PowerShell 0.8.1 and 0.8.2
content: These two Azure PowerShell releases include support and updates for: Managed Cache - manage your cache and regenerate access keys Azure Automation - manage your automation account, runbook, jobs, and schedule Traffic Manager - manage your profile and endpoints Anti-Malware Cloud Service extension - new management tools for the anti-malware extension Virtual Machines and Networking - manage public IP, reserved IP, internal load balancer, VM image disks, and virtual network gateway keys

title: General Availability: Import/Export
content: Move large amounts of data into and out of Azure Blobs by sending your hard drives directly to an Azure datacenter. This is usually much faster and cheaper than uploading or downloading data from the Internet. Check out Import/Export pricing options , or get started right away.

title: General Availability: VNET-to-VNET connections for virtual networks
content: Directly and securely connect multiple virtual networks using VNET to VNET connections. Your VNETs can be running in different Azure regions, but still have all traffic routed using the Azure backbone. All data flowing between VNETs is charged at the same rate as egress traffic. VNET to VNET connections work great if you require a presence in multiple regions, highly available applications, or the integration of VNETs for a larger network. Check out the Virtual Network and pricing pages to get started.

title: General Availability: Managed Cache Service
content: Azure Managed Cache Service is a highly secured, dedicated cache that’s managed by Microsoft. It provides high performance and is easy to use in your cloud applications. A cache created using the Azure Cache Service is accessible from any application within Azure that’s running on Azure Web Sites, Cloud Services, or Virtual Machines. For more information, visit the Azure Cache page. To get a comprehensive look at pricing, visit the Cache Pricing Details page.

title: Windows 7 and Windows 8.1 client VM images are now available for MSDN subscribers
content: Virtual machine images for Windows 7 and Windows 8.1 are now available in the Azure virtual machine gallery. MSDN subscribers now have the flexibility to utilize an on-demand dev/test environment for their client-targeted app, leveraging the elasticity and scale of Microsoft Azure. To get started, log in to the Azure Management Portal and create a new Virtual Machine.

title: Preview: Azure Media Services Live Streaming and Content Protection
content: The same live streaming solution that seamlessly delivered the 2014 Winter Olympics and 2014 FIFA World Cup to broadcasters around the world is now available in preview. To protect premium video content, we've introduced Content Protection with static and dynamic encryption and a range of industry-standard encryption options like PlayReady DRM and Clearkey AES. Make your audio and video files accessible and easy to discover with Indexer (now generally available). For more information, please visit the Media Services webpage. For a comprehensive look at pricing, visit the Media Services Pricing Details webpage.

title: Azure PowerShell 0.8.8
content: This Azure PowerShell release includes: Role-based access control support Query role definition Get-AzureRoleDefinition Manage role assignment New-AzureRoleAssignment Get-AzureRoleAssignment Remove-AzureRoleAssignment Query Active Directory object Get-AzureADUser Get-AzureADGroup Get-AzureADGroupMember Get-AzureADServicePrincipal Show user's permissions on Get-AzureResourceGroup Get-AzureResource Active Directory service principal login support in Azure Resource Manager mode Add-AzureAccount -Credential -ServicePrincipal -Tenant SQL Database auditing support in Azure Resource Manager mode Use-AzureSqlServerAuditingSetting Set-AzureSqlServerAuditingSetting Set-AzureSqlDatabaseAuditingSetting Get-AzureSqlServerAuditingSetting Get-AzureSqlDatabaseAuditingSetting Disable-AzureSqlServerAuditing Disable-AzureSqlDatabaseAuditing Other improvements Virtual Machine DSC extension supports configuration argument Virtual Machine Antimalware extension supports native JSON configuration Storage supports creating storage account with different geo-redundant options Traffic Manager supports nesting of profiles Website supports configuring x32/x64 worker process -Detail parameter on Get-AzureResourceGroup to improve performance Major refactoring around account and subscription management

title: Authenticate to Azure from Azure Automation using Azure Active Directory
content: Azure Automation no longer requires management certificates to automate Azure resources. Now you can automate the management of your Azure services simply by creating an Azure Active Directory user (an OrgId). This feature is included in Azure PowerShell Version 0.8.6, which introduced the ability to noninteractively authenticate to Azure using an OrgId user. To learn more about how you can use this new feature, see Azure Automation: Authenticating to Azure using Azure Active Directory . Azure Automation is a new service that allows you to automate the management of resources in your Azure environment using a highly scalable and reliable workflow execution engine. Not an Azure Automation user yet? Sign up for the preview and then check out the Getting Started Guide .

title: Manage your Azure Websites directly with Websites Process Explorer
content: Use Process Explorer to manage your website processes, and you'll be able to enumerate different instances of your site, browse processes for each instance, and drill down and view the handles and modules associated with each process. You'll also get get rich monitoring of the CPU, Working Set, and Thread count at the process level to help you identify runaway processes, find open file handles, and even kill a specific process instance.

title: Preview: Azure Cosmos DB
content: Azure Cosmos DB is the highly scalable NoSQL document database-as-a-service that offers rich query and transactional processing over schema-free data. It helps deliver configurable and reliable performance and enables rapid development. This is all through a self-managed platform and is backed by the power and reach of Azure. Azure Cosmos DB is the right solution for web and mobile applications when predictable throughput, low latency, and flexible query are key. Offered in combinable units that include dedicated throughput and storage to meet the performance and storage needs of your application, Azure Cosmos DB enables you to quickly build, grow, and scale cloud applications. It’s designed for the cloud to enable rapid development and iteration. Robust data storage, integrated transactional JavaScript processing, and rich querying are delivered using industry-standard developer technologies such as JavaScript, RESTful APIs over HTTP, and a native JSON data model. This approach empowers developers to bring their application, data, and existing knowledge to build modern web and mobile applications. Azure Cosmos DB is available in the Azure Preview portal . During public preview, Azure Cosmos DB will be offered at a discount in all regions where the service is available. For more information, read about Azure Cosmos DB on the SQL Server Blog or visit the Azure Cosmos DB webpage. For a comprehensive look at pricing, visit the Azure Cosmos DB Pricing Details webpage.

title: StorSimple Available In Japan East and West
content: StorSimple is now available in Japan East and Japan West with the same service-level agreement coverage available in other regions worldwide. StorSimple offers a unique hybrid cloud storage solution which provides large on-premises capacity for SSD and HDD, data protection, as well as data mobility through access to enterprise data in Microsoft Azure through the StorSimple Virtual Appliance. This solution optimizes total storage costs and data protection for enterprises, with consolidated management through Azure portal. For more information about services regional availability, please visit our Azure Regions page .

title: Azure Backup Available In Japan East and Japan West
content: Azure Backup is now available in Japan East and Japan West with the same service-level agreement coverage available in other regions worldwide. Azure Backup can help you back up and recover data across Windows Server and Microsoft System Center. You can store and recover files, SQL Server database snapshots, and Hyper-V virtual machines in the cloud. For more information about services' regional availability, visit our Azure Regions page .

title: Preview: Azure Search
content: Azure Search is a search-as-a-service solution that allows developers to incorporate search capabilities into their applications without having to worry about the complexities of full-text search or to deploy, maintain or manage any infrastructure. Even as non-experts, developers can construct rich ranking models that connect search results to application or business objectives. For more information, see Azure Search overview . For a comprehensive look at pricing, see Azure Search Pricing Details .

title: Server management experiences for SQL Database
content: In this update, we have added server management experiences for SQL Database in the new Azure Preview portal. You can now easily reset the server administrator password, and configure firewall rules and default auditing settings for databases in the server.

title: General Availability: Mobile Services .NET backend
content: The Mobile Services .NET backend is generally available. With a .NET backend, you can write your services using the power of ASP.NET Web API and your favorite .NET language. Mobile Services lets you add a cloud-hosted backend to your mobile app and quickly light up functionality such as data storage, authentication, and scalable push notifications. For more information, check out the announcement blog post from Scott Guthrie .

title: Create and manage Azure WebJobs in the Azure Preview portal
content: Azure WebJobs can now be created and managed in the Azure Portal preview. The portal will support On Demand WebJobs and Continuous WebJobs. This feature is accessible in the portal on the Website blade and through the WebJobs button, which opens the WebJobs blade. You can also use the Console to interact with your WebJobs directly, and use the WebJobs SDK to make authoring easier. Learn more about Azure WebJobs .

title: Azure Site Recovery Available In Japan East and Japan West
content: Azure Site Recovery is now available in Japan East and Japan West with the same service-level agreement coverage available in other regions worldwide. Azure Site Recovery can help you protect important applications by coordinating the replication and recovery of private clouds across sites, whether you’re protecting dozens or hundreds of virtual machines. You can protect your applications to your own second site, a hoster’s site, or even use Azure as your disaster recovery site (preview) and avoid the expense and complexity of building and managing your own secondary location. For more information about services' regional availability, visit our Azure Regions page .

title: Azure commercially available in 51 additional countries
content: We have added 51 countries where customers can use credit cards to purchase Azure and deploy services. See the full list of countries where Azure is commercially available.

title: General Availability: Azure HDInsight in Japan West and US Central
content: Azure HDInsight is now generally available in the Japan West and US Central regions, meaning you can host HDInsight in those regions with the same service-level agreement coverage available in other regions around the world. Japan West and US Central are the latest HDInsight regions, joining US North Central, US South Central, and Asia Pacific East. The HDInsight Pricing Details page has been updated with geography-specific pricing for Japan West.

title: Azure Resource Manager Tools Preview (Visual Studio 2013)
content: Azure Resource Manager Tools Preview for Visual Studio 2013 enables developers to create reusable deployment templates (JSON files) that declaratively describe the resources that make up an app. Tooling to validate and deploy these deployment templates is also provided. For example, a deployment template may include a website, Redis cache, SQL Azure database, and other resources. This simplifies the process of creating complex environments for development, testing, and production in a repeatable manner and provides a unified way to manage and monitor the resources that make up an app from the Azure Preview portal. Read more about the Azure Resource Manager Tools Preview for Visual Studio 2013 on the Azure Blog .

title: MyGet available in the Microsoft Azure Store
content: MyGet provides hosted NuGet servers. Developers can use their own packages to create and host NuGet feeds, or use another package source (such as NuGet.org). MyGet already provides a popular integration with Visual Studio Online . Now developers can manage packages in one portal alongside their Azure services. If you're a Microsoft Azure customer, here’s how to create a new MyGet account: Go to the Microsoft Azure Management Portal . In the bottom toolbar, click New and then click Store . In the Choose an Add-on box, click MyGet and then click Next . In the Personalize Add-on box, choose the MyGet plan you want to sign up for. If you want to create one (or more) paid subscriptions, use the promotional code STORELAUNCH . You'll get a 25 percent discount during the first six months of the subscription (the code is valid until end of August 2014). After the subscription is created, click Manage in the bottom toolbar and then create a username and password for your subscription. Happy packaging!

title: Azure SDK 2.4 and Visual Studio 2013 Update 3 are available for download
content: Visual Studio 2013 Update 3 and Azure SDK 2.4 for .NET are now available for download with various Azure development tooling features: Visual Studio Update 3 [ download ] Websites : Publish WebJobs from Console or Web projects. Mobile Services : Create a Dev/Test environment in the cloud when creating Mobile Services projects. Use the Push Notification Wizard with .NET Mobile Services. Notification Hubs : View and manage device registrations. Azure SDK 2.4 for .NET [ VS 2013 download | VS 2012 download ] With the additional installation of the Azure SDK 2.4 for .NET, you can also take advantage of the following features: Virtual Machines : Remote debug 32-bit Virtual Machines. Configure Virtual Machines, including installation and configuration of dynamic extensions (for example, anti-malware, Puppet, Chef, and custom script). Create Virtual Machine snapshots of the disk state. Storage : View Storage activity logs for diagnostics. Provision Read-Access Geo-redundant Storage from Visual Studio. Cloud Services : Emulator Express is the default option for new projects (Full Emulator is deprecated). Configure new networking capabilities in the service model. Read more about it on the Azure blog .

title: Azure PowerShell 0.8.6
content: This Azure PowerShell release includes: Non-interactive login support for Microsoft organizational accounts with Add-AzureAccount -Credential Cloud service cmdlet upgrades to Azure SDK 2.4 Compute updates: PowerShell DSC VM extension Get-AzureVMDscExtension Remove-AzureVMDscExtension Set-AzureVMDscExtension Publish-AzureVMDscConfiguration Added CompanyName and SupportedOS parameters to Publish-AzurePlatformExtension New-AzureVM will display a warning instead of an error when the service already exists in the same subscription Added Version parameter to generic service extension cmdlets Changed the ShowInGUI parameter to DoNotShowInGUI in Update-AzureVMImage SQL Database updates: Added OfflineSecondary parameter to Start-AzureSqlDatabaseCopy Database copy cmdlets will return two more properties: IsOfflineSecondary and IsTerminationAllowed Windows Azure Pack updates: New-WAPackCloudService Get-WAPackCloudService Remove-WAPackCloudService New-WAPackVMRole Get-WAPackVMRole Set-WAPackVMRole Remove-WAPackVMRole New-WAPackVNet Remove-WAPackVNet New-WAPackVMSubnet Get-WAPackVMSubnet Remove-WAPackVMSubnet New-WAPackStaticIPAddressPool Get-WAPackStaticIPAddressPool Remove-WAPackStaticIPAddressPool Get-WAPackLogicalNetwork You can download and install the Azure PowerShell modules through Microsoft Web Platform Installer .

title: RavenDB on Azure available in the Azure Store
content: RavenHQ Database is the official hosted solution for RavenDB. A fully managed cloud of RavenDB servers running in Azure and a variety of scalable plans means you’ll never have to worry about installation, updates, availability, performance, security, or backups again. To get started: Log in to the Azure Portal . In the lower pane of the management portal, click New . Click Store . In the Choose an Add-on dialog, select RavenHQ Database and click the right arrow. In the Personalize Add-on dialog, select the RavenHQ Database plan you want to sign up for. Provision your RavenHQ Database in seconds and it’s ready to use!

title: MemCachier memcache-as-a-service available in the Azure Store
content: MemCachier manages and scales clusters of memcache servers so that you can focus on your app. Their custom memcache implementation offers better reliability and usability than memcached, with the same low latency. Select from a variety of plans (including a free 25 MB cache plan), and add capacity when you need it without changing any code. To get started: Log in to the Azure Portal . In the lower pane of the management portal, click New . Click Store . In the Choose an Add-on dialog, select MemCachier and click the right arrow. In the Personalize Add-on dialog, select the MemCachier plan you want to sign up for. Provision your MemCachier service in seconds and it’s ready to use!

title: Azure Brazil South region now in public preview
content: The Azure Brazil South region, located in Sao Paulo state, is broadly available for public preview (the final step before general availability). The new region means better performance and reduced latency for local customers, who can now keep their data in country if they opt for Locally Redundant Storage . While the region is in public preview, standard supplemental terms of use for Azure previews apply, meaning the Brazil South region (and all services hosted there) are excluded from service level agreements during the preview period. Billing and subscription management support will be provided at no additional cost, and paid Azure support plans will be honored. The Azure website has been updated to provide detailed information on service availability and pricing for the new region. Azure Virtual Machines, Cloud Services, Storage, SQL Database, Web Sites, and Data Transfers hosted from Brazil South will be offered at a discount during the preview period.

title: New Azure Web Sites region – Southeast Asia
content: Azure Web Sites recently expanded to Japan, and now we're adding Southeast Asia to our list of supported regions. Starting today, all customers will have the options to create their websites in the new region, with all Azure Web Sites’ great features available from day one. With the addition of this region, Azure Websites is now available in 4 different Asia regions: East Asia, Japan West, Japan East and Southeast Asia.

title: Redis support on Azure available in the Azure Store
content: Redis Labs is now offering Redis Cloud in the Azure Store . Redis Cloud is a fully-managed cloud service for hosting and running your Redis dataset in a highly-available and scalable manner, with predictable and stable top performance. Redis Cloud offers true high-availability with its in-memory dataset replication and instant auto-failover mechanism, combined with its fast storage engine. Import an existing dataset to any of your Redis Cloud databases, from Azure blobs storage, FTP/HTTP server, or from any other Redis server. Daily backups are performed automatically, or you can backup your dataset manually any time you want to. The service guarantees the same high performance as the strongest cloud instances. Redis Cloud offers several price tiers, including a free plan with 1 dedicated database. To get started: Login to the Azure Management Portal . In the lower pane of the management portal, click New . Click Store . In the Choose an Add-on dialog, select Redis Cloud and click the right arrow. In the Personalize Add-on dialog, select the Redis Cloud plan you want to sign up for. Provision your Redis Cloud DB in seconds and it's ready to use!

title: Cluster Operating System Update for HDInsight Clusters
content: HDInsight clusters created after April 3, 2014, have the following changes: Windows Server 2012 R2 (Azure OS Family 4) as the default OS on the cluster .NET 4.5 Updates to internal firewall rules Windows Server 2012 R2 This update moves HDInsight clusters to the most recent version of the OS. This enables greater performance and reliability, as well as the ability to integrate with OS features specific to OS Family 4 . .NET 4.5 As part of Windows Server 2012 R2, clusters now have .NET 4.5 available for use when submitting .NET Map/Reduce , LINQ to Hive , or .NET Streaming. This also enables the usage of the research prototype for Dryad and Naiad Updates to Internal Cluster Firewall Rules Previously, inbound connections on cluster nodes (within the cluster) were constrained to executables hosted via java.exe. We have relaxed this restriction, allowing inbound connections to any executable on worker nodes. This is only for traffic within the cluster, there are no changes to external endpoints. An HDInsight has one external endpoint for leveraging the REST API's.

title: General Availability: Autoscale
content: Autoscale is now generally available. We've added new features since we first released it as a preview version: support for both performance- and schedule-based autoscaling, along with an API and .NET SDK so you can scale by any performance counters that you define. Autoscale supports all four Azure compute services: Cloud Services, Virtual Machines, Mobile Services and Web Sites. For Virtual Machines and Web Sites, Autoscale is included as a feature in the Standard mode, and for Mobile Services, it's included as a part of both Basic and Standard modes. There's no additional charge for Autoscale, besides the cost for the underlying compute service.

title: General Availability: Azure Read-Access Geo Redundant Storage (RA-GRS)
content: Geo Redundant Storage accounts store data in two separate regions: The primary region (the default location where all updates and deletes are kept), and a secondary region (where copies of your data are stored). When you enable Azure Read-Access Geo Redundant Storage (RA-GRS), your application has Read-only access to the secondary region’s copy of the data in case your primary storage location fails.

title: Azure Management Library 2.0.0-Preview for .NET and Node.js
content: In this preview release of Azure Management Library for .NET and Node.js, we're adding support for Azure Resource Manager. Create, manage, and deploy resource groups using local or gallery templates, search for and download gallery templates, and create and manage individual resources.

title: General Availability: Scheduler
content: Azure Scheduler is live, available in all Azure regions, backed by an enterprise SLA, and ready to use for production scenarios. The release also includes new Azure Scheduler PowerShell cmdlets, and the Scheduler .NET API (included in WAML 1.0 ). Our customers used Scheduler (Preview) to invoke Hadoop workloads, trigger diagnostic cleanups, and periodically check that partners have submitted content on time. ISVs used it to add scheduling capabilities, like report generation and send reminders. Use Azure Scheduler to run jobs on simple or complex recurring schedules that can invoke HTTP/S endpoints or post messages to storage queues. Scheduler has built-in high availability and can reliably call services inside or outside of Azure. Azure Scheduler documentation .NET API NuGet Package Download Azure PowerShell MSDN forum to find answers to all your Scheduler questions Scheduler Pricing Details page

title: Azure Cross Platform Command-Line Interface 0.8.0
content: In this release of Azure Cross Platform Command-Line Interface, we're adding support for Azure Resource Manager and Azure Active Directory authentication. Azure Resource Management support includes creating, managing, and deploying resource groups using local or gallery templates, search and download functionality for gallery templates, and creating and managing individual resources. Azure Active Directory authentication updates let you log in with a username and password from the console for an organizational account.

title: New in Azure Web Sites: Web Hosting Plans
content: You can now create web hosting plans that let you share features like auto-scale, web tests, backup, and computing capacity across your web sites. Web hosting plans support a few pricing tiers (Free, Shared, Basic, and Standard) where each tier has its own capabilities. Sites in the same subscription and geographic location can share a web hosting plan. You can choose to have sites share a web hosting plan, or you can dedicate a web hosting plan to an individual site if that site requires dedicated Learn more about Web Hosting Plans .

title: New Basic SKU for Azure Web Sites
content: We've added a new Basic SKU tier (in addition to our current Free, Standard and Shared tiers) for customers who need more than the Shared tier offers. It includes scaling up to 3 dedicated instances, staging slots, and support for SSL. Plus, you'll run on a dedicated VM, but at a lower price than the Standard tier. If you need support for more instances (10), more shared storage (50 GB), site slots, or backup and restore, upgrade to the Standard tier.

title: Resource groups in Azure Preview portal
content: Resource groups are a new concept in the Azure Preview portal. We think of them as "lifecycle boundaries," because when resources share a resource group, their lifecycles (from create, to update, to delete) are managed in an integrated way. Use resource groups to collect and manage all your application resources. Link resources across resource groups, share resources across lifecycle boundaries, and manage costs. View, monitor, and track your usage and billing for all the resources your application uses. New visuals show you every resource in the group, including any resources that are linked across groups. Learn more about using Resource groups in the Preview portal .

title: New monitoring and operations features in Azure Web Sites
content: The Azure Portal preview adds new monitoring features for Azure Web Sites, including: View your site's streaming logs, and open a console to run commands against your site. Learn more . Create autoscale rules that use different metrics, and set up multiple scale-up or -down rules for the same metric. Learn more . Monitor memory working set (in bytes, per website), CPU percentage, memory percentage, HTTP queue length, and disk queue length to solve performance problems. Customize the charts in the Preview portal with the metrics that matter to you, choose different time ranges, and clone charts for side-by-side comparison. Learn more . Get a full event history of all of the operations in your service, including your initial deployment, changes made to resources, and alerts on the health of your service. Learn more . Create web tests to monitor the uptime and performance of your website from different locations around the globe. Learn more . Analytics that track the users of your site, including what browsers and devices they use, what pages they visit, and the performance of those pages. Learn more .

title: Puppet Extension is now available for Azure
content: Puppet Enterprise is IT automation software that gives system administrators the power to easily automate repetitive tasks, quickly deploy critical applications, and proactively manage infrastructure. The Puppet Agent installed with this Azure extension fetches configurations from a Puppet Master server, and reports events to the Puppet Enterprise Console, a graphical interface that visualizes infrastructure changes across the organization. This extension is published by Puppet Labs .

title: New Azure billing features
content: Billing is now part of every service blade in the Preview portal. We’ve created Billing journeys that help you slice and dice your billing info and turn it into charts and visualizations that give you at-a-glance insights into each of your subscriptions. When you open your Start board, you’ll see a high-level summary of your subscriptions. Dive into the Billing summary to see overall subscription status, the current charges over time, and the next due date for running charges. Individual subscription data includes status, cost over time, cost by resources breakdown, and other details.

title: Visual Studio Online is now integrated with the Azure portal
content: Manage your development lifecycle with Visual Studio Online in the Azure portal. Create a Team Project to collaborate with others, host your source code, track work items, monitor builds, and continuously deploy to Azure Websites. Start your next development project in the cloud – 5 users are free! Learn more

title: First-of-its-kind Microsoft Azure Preview portal
content: The Azure Preview portal's all-in-one, work-anywhere experience combines developer and infrastructure services to radically simplify DevOps, whether you write code, operate infrastructure, or manage finances. To learn more about the Preview portal, check out this 3 minute video .

title: Azure Active Directory App Gallery
content: Add and manage over 1000 apps using Azure Active Directory. Check out the list of apps , or add an app using the Azure Management portal to see it in the app gallery.

title: New service: Automation (Preview)
content: Use Azure Automation (now in public preview) to create, monitor, deploy, and maintain resources in your Azure environment. It automates time-consuming, error-prone, and frequently repeated cloud operations tasks (for both Azure and third party systems). Visit Scott Guthrie’s blog and the Automation page to learn more about Automation and how to get started.

title: Standard tier pricing changes for Azure Web Sites
content: Now that we've introduced the Basic pricing tier, we're making some improvements to the Standard tier. We're increasing the storage quota from 10 GB to 50 GB, adding 5 free SNI SSL and dedicated IP to each subscription, and removing the Web Socket 350 connection limit. Changes take effect in April 2014.

title: Java support on Microsoft Azure Web Sites
content: Beginning in April, Azure Web Sites supports hosting Java web applications. You won't have to make a ton of configuration changes - when you're done, you can send all incoming site HTTP traffic to the Java HTTP listen port. Use the Azure Portal to create Java 7 websites with Apache Tomcat 7.0.50 or Jetty 9.1.0 and upload a .WAR file. Get more advanced with complete installs of Apache Tomcat or Jetty (available in the application gallery), and create a web container you can configure for your website.

title: Wildcard domains in Azure Web Sites
content: Combine wildcard domains with SNI SSL to secure all your subdomains, without creating individual bindings. To add a wildcard hostname, point a wildcard CNAME record to your site just like you would for a regular hostname (e.g., "*.contoso.com"). Then use Azure's domain configuration to add that domain to your site.

title: Irregular sign-in notifications added to Azure Active Directory Premium
content: Azure Active Directory identifies your normal user sign-in patterns. When a sign-in falls outside the norm, it's included in a report and your administrators are notified. Learn more about these notifications (and other reporting and analytics tools in Azure Active Directory and Azure Active Directory Premium) in the Active Directory team blog .

title: Azure PowerShell 0.8.0
content: In this release of Azure PowerShell, we're adding support for Azure Resource Manager, Scheduler and a bunch of infrastructure cmdlet improvements. Azure Resource Management support includes creating and managing resource groups and resource group deployments using local or gallery templates, search and download functionality for gallery templates, and creating and managing individual resources. Azure Scheduler support includes creating and managing job collections and HTTP and storage queue jobs. Infrastructure cmdlet improvements include VM custom script extension support and VM image support.

title: VM Images replace OS Images
content: VM Image is the new and improved image entity and replaces OS Images. It includes the OS disk, and adds data disks. Capture a VM (running or shut down) to create a VM Image. The underlying operating system may be generalized (for example, sys prep has been run for Windows or `waagent –deprovision’ executed for Linux - like an OS Image today), or specialized (where the provisioning information remains intact). Once captured, use a VM Image to deploy new VMs. Think of the generalized VM Image as a model you can use to use to stamp out similar VMs, and the specialized VM Image as a snapshot of the disks used to deploy a VM to a known good point in time.

title: Azure Active Directory Premium
content: You can subscribe to Azure Active Directory Premium starting today. Azure Active Directory Premium subscribers can leverage: Self-service password reset Self-service group management Group-based application access management Multi-factor authentication Customized branding Reporting, alerting and analytics Learn more about Azure Active Direct Premium (including how to subscribe) on the Active Directory team blog .

title: Management Libraries for .NET
content: The Management Libraries for .NET include managed wrappers around the Microsoft Azure Service Management REST APIs . These libraries give .NET developers a client-side SDK written as Portable Class Libraries (PCL), so if you're writing applications for desktop applications in .NET, Windows 8.1 Store applications, or Windows Phone 8 applications, you can automate the provisioning or management of Microsoft Azure assets. Use the Management Libraries for .NET to write integration tests that provision environments in Microsoft Azure (and destroy them when your tests complete), enable Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solutions to spin up new Web Sites or Cloud Services, or to get deep information about the running state of their assets. Tasks previously available only via the Management Portal are now exposed to .NET developers in a set of easily-discoverable client APIs. The following areas of Azure will be available in the Management Libraries for .NET in the 1.0 release of the NuGet packages: Web Sites Cloud Services Storage Monitoring Scheduler Media Services Networks Over the next few months we'll be adding other asset types to the Management Libraries (and announcing them on the Service Updates blog), so stay tuned.

title: Azure Active Directory Premium: Self-service group management
content: Self-service group management is now available to Azure Active Directory Premium subscribers. Your employees can add and manage cloud based security groups, and these groups can be used to assign access to applications. Learn more on the Active Directory team blog .

title: General Availability: Azure in China
content: We've partnered with 21Vianet - one of the largest Internet service providers in China - to bring Azure's public cloud services to Chinese customers. Visit the Official Microsoft Blog for more information on today’s announcement.

title: General Availability: Hadoop 2 in Azure HDInsight
content: Hadoop 2.2 in Azure HDInsight is now generally available. Easily deploy the latest version of key Hadoop components (including YARN, Hive, Pig, Oozie and others) to Azure and bring big data processing to all of the data in Azure Blob Storage. This release includes improved performance and scalability of the core Map/Reduce implementation, the ability to use YARN to bring different distributed apps to the cluster, and substantial performance improvements in Hive via the second phase of the Stinger Project . To get started, head to the management portal and deploy a version 3 cluster using Custom Create . Or, see Get started Hadoop in HDInsight .

title: Reduced Pricing on Storage
content: We're reducing prices by up to 20% for Block Blobs Storage and Disks/Page Blobs Storage, up to 28% for Locally Redundant Disks/Page Blobs Storage, and reducing the price of Azure Storage transactions by 50%. These pricing reductions are in effect for all regions worldwide. Learn more on the Azure Storage pricing page .

title: General Availability: Oracle software on Azure
content: Oracle Database, Oracle WebLogic Server, and Java are now generally available with license-included virtual machine images, and you can find them in the Azure Virtual Machines image gallery. Whether you’re an Oracle administrator or a Java developer, you have full Oracle support. Learn more at Azure.com .

title: Azure Traffic Manager now supports Azure Web Sites
content: Azure Traffic Manager is extending support to manage and load balance Azure Web sites. This feature is available for all web sites in the Standard tier. This integration brings the benefits of Traffic Manager, previously available only for Cloud Services, to Azure Web sites-based deployments. Key Traffic Manager scenarios now enabled for Azure Web sites include: High availability : Use multiple deployments in separate data centers, with built-in health monitoring and automatic failover Improved performance : By geo-distributing deployments in Azure data centers in multiple locations, and routing end users to their closest deployment, latency is reduced and the end-user experience improved Seamless upgrade : Take one deployment offline, whilst using Traffic Manager to route user traffic to a different deployment In addition, you can combine Cloud Services and Azure Websites in a single Traffic Manager policy. This enables new scenarios such as failover to an Azure Web sites-based holding page if your Cloud Service is unavailable. For details on how to use this feature, see Traffic Manager on MSDN

title: New Azure datacenters available in Japan
content: We've opened two new Azure datacenters in Japan: Japan East (in Saitama Prefecture) and Japan West (in Osaka Prefecture). Both officially launched in February and were built to help customers meet data residency goals, improve data durability, and address disaster recovery scenarios via geo-replication between the two regions. Visit the Microsoft Azure website for details on service availability and pricing . Read the Official Microsoft Blog for more background info on the launch.

title: Azure Web Sites now supports WebJobs
content: Run custom jobs (using executables or scripts) on your web site. WebJobs supports running jobs on demand, continuously, or on a schedule, and automates administrative or recurring tasks. See How to Use the WebJobs feature in Azure Web Sites to learn more.

title: Service Health Notifications added to the Management Portal
content: Azure Incident Notifications now displayed within the Azure Management Portal. Customers will see a toast in the Portal for the following major types of ongoing (i.e. “Active”) incidents, with the option to open a pop-up with more information about the incident. Partial Performance Degradation Partial Service Interruption Full Performance Degradation Full Service Interruption Advisory Learn more about Azure Service Notifications .

title: Remove standard server headers in Azure Web Sites
content: HTTP headers are part of the communication process between web servers and browsers, and are included in the request and response. One example is the server header, which lists the product name and version of the web server (e.g., Microsoft-IIS/8.0 ). All web servers generate these headers, but now you can disable them on Azure Web Sites. You need to update your site’s web.config file to remove headers. Learn how on the Azure team blog .

title: Backup and restore for Azure Web Sites
content: Save a snapshot version of your web app (along with any SQL or MySQL databases it uses) and start your site backup. You decide when a backup starts - manually, or automatically on a schedule you choose (for example, once a day at midnight). Later, restore a website to a previous version, or create a new website based on one of your original site's backups. Backup and Restore is available at no additional cost to all Web Site customers using our Standard Tier.

title: New extension shows virtual machine info
content: The recent VM Agent release includes an extension that displays Windows virtual machine info on the desktop of the VM instance (when you RDP into it). It's a quick way to see VM configuration settings (internal and public IP, disk space, memory, deployment ID, etc).

title: New service: ExpressRoute (Preview)
content: ExpressRoute (now in public preview) is a dedicated, private, high-throughput network connection between Azure datacenters and on-premises IT environments. Connect your existing datacenters to Azure without flowing any traffic over the public Internet. Network quality-of-service is guaranteed. Use Azure as a natural extension of an existing private network or datacenter. Start today with dedicated connections though Equinix datacenters, add Azure services to MPLS VPN provided by AT&T, or (through a new strategic partnership with Level3) create a private connection with Level3 Cloud Connect Solutions. Visit Scott Guthrie's blog to learn more about ExpressRoute and how to configure connections to your local networks. Check out the ExpressRoute page for getting started content and FAQs.
